brief.summary: This study reveals highly conserved mitochondrial genome architecture of Culex pipiens form pipiens from the Turkish Black Sea region, with high variability in selected loci and terminal regions.
brief.objective: To investigate the mitogenomic diversity and phylogenetic relationships within Culex pipiens complex through sequencing and comparative analysis of complete mitochondrial genomes.
brief.timeline_geography: 2024, Black Sea region, Turkey
brief.population_sample: Five Turkish Culex pipiens form pipiens isolates collected from different provinces along the Turkish Black Sea coast.
brief.key_methods: Sequencing and assembly of complete mitochondrial genomes with a strong A+T bias (~78.2%) and typical set of 37 mitochondrial genes.
key_findings: Highly conserved mitogenome architecture
Mitochondrial diversity concentrated in selected loci (COX1, ND2, COX3, CYTB, ND5, and 12S rRNA) and terminal regions
Turkish isolates do not form a single exclusive mitochondrial lineage
brief.discussion: The findings support the view that mitochondrial genomes in this complex primarily reflect maternal lineage history and may be influenced by introgression and incomplete lineage sorting rather than sharply discrete taxonomic or form-level boundaries.
brief.limitations: The study's limited sample size and geographical scope
brief.recommendations: Future comparative and evolutionary studies should incorporate additional mitogenomic resources from diverse geographical locations and consider the implications of maternal lineage complexity within the broader complex.

brief.summary: The study investigates how West Nile Virus NS3 helicase regulates RNA binding through allosteric coupling between motif V and VI. Researchers used microsecond-scale simulations to analyze the dynamic interaction between E413 in motif V and R461 in motif VIL, which affects RNA affinity.
brief.objective: To understand the underlying mechanism of NS3 helicase's RNA-binding regulation and identify opportunities for structure-based antiviral design.
brief.timeline_geography: no specific mention of time or place
brief.population_sample: West Nile Virus NS3 helicase protein
brief.key_methods: microsecond-scale all-atom molecular dynamics simulations, nonbonded linear interaction energy (E inter) calculation, Pearson's correlation, hydrogen bond analysis
key_findings: the dynamic interaction between E413 in motif V and R461 in motif VIL modulates RNA binding affinity.
mutations of D471 affect this interaction and impair hydrolysis.
brief.discussion: The findings provide mechanistic insights into NS3h function and identify new opportunities for structure-based antiviral design. The study highlights the complex interplay between nucleotide and RNA binding during the hydrolysis cycle.
brief.limitations: none mentioned
brief.recommendations: structure-based antiviral drug design targeting motif VIL or its interactions with E413.

brief.summary: Research on WNV infection has revealed the importance of gamma delta T cells in controlling viral dissemination and their potential as antiviral targets.
brief.objective: To discuss recent studies on the role of gamma delta T cells in viral pathogenesis and protective immunity during WNV infection
brief.timeline_geography: Worldwide; focus on Europe, Africa, Asia, North and South America
brief.population_sample: Humans, birds, mosquitoes
brief.key_methods: Cell cultures, animal models (hamsters, mice, monkeys, horses)
key_findings: Gamma delta T cells play a critical role in controlling WNV infection.
Gamma delta T cells can recognize non-peptidic antigens called Phosphoantigens (PhAgs)
Host immunity reacts quickly and non-specifically to WNV infections
brief.discussion: The importance of gamma delta T cells in controlling WNV infection is still unclear. Further research on the mechanisms of gamma delta T cell activation during WNV infection is needed.

brief.summary: This study develops sensitive real-time PCR assays to detect West Nile virus (WNV) and Usutu virus (USUV) in bird and human samples in Finland, finding no positivity despite nearby infections and introducing the risk of future introduction and need for continued surveillance.
brief.objective: The aim was to develop specific diagnostic methods for detecting WNV and USUV nucleic acids and investigating evidence of virus circulation and seroprevalence of these viruses in wild birds in Finland.
brief.timeline_geography: Summer months, 2020, Korkeasaari Zoo Wildlife Hospital in Finland
brief.population_sample: 163 deceased bird samples (N = 34 migratory species) and 337 human serum samples collected during the summer
brief.key_methods: Real-time PCR assays for WNV and USUV nucleic acids developed, optimized and evaluated using bird and human samples. Indirect Immunofluorescence Assay (IFA) used to detect anti-WNV IgG antibodies in bird samples.
key_findings: WNV-RT-qPCR had high sensitivity with limits of detection of 13.0 copies per reaction for WNV and 14.6 copies per reaction for USUV
No positive samples detected for either virus.
Bird samples tested negative for anti-WNV antibodies.
brief.discussion: Although no positive samples were detected, the risk of future introduction of WNV into Finland is highlighted by active migratory bird flyways from Africa and Southern/Central Europe and recent cases in neighbouring countries. The authors suggest continued surveillance and availability of efficient diagnostic tools as essential for preparedness.

brief.summary: This paper discovers and mutasynthesizes ansatrienin B, a broad-spectrum inhibitor against RNA viruses, which shows potential in treating COVID-19.
brief.objective: The authors aim to discover and optimize a new compound with broad-spectrum inhibitory activity against RNA viruses.
brief.timeline_geography: China, 2026
brief.population_sample: African green monkey kidney cell line Vero E6, human epithelial colorectal adenocarcinoma cell line Caco-2, and human cervical cancer cells overexpressing human ACE2 (Hela-ACE2)
brief.key_methods: PCR amplifications, SPR assays, IF assay, RT-qPCR
key_findings: Ansatrienin B inhibits SARS-CoV-2 infection with an IC50 of 0.078 μmol/L.
The compound reduces viral loads and modulates inflammatory cytokines/chemokines in Vero E6 cells.

brief.summary: This study monitored vector-borne diseases in Italy and Greece by collecting and analyzing mosquitoes from various regions.
brief.objective: To investigate the distribution and prevalence of mosquito-borne pathogens in Italy and Greece, informing public health strategies and disease prevention measures.
brief.timeline_geography: 2022-23, Italy (Marche and Umbria regions) and 2023, Crete Island, Greece
brief.population_sample: Mosquitoes collected from 145 sites in Marche (54), Umbria (19), Heraklion (7), and Rethymno (7) across urban, peri-urban, rural, and wetland areas.
brief.key_methods: Mosquito sampling with CDC CO2 traps in Italy and BG-Sentinel 2 traps in Crete; Morphological and molecular identification of mosquito species.
key_findings: Presence of Culex pipiens and Ae. albopictus in both regions, with highest abundances found in Marche, Italy.

brief.summary: A case of severe West Nile virus infection with septic shock and acute kidney injury (AKI) led to chronic kidney disease (CKD) Stage 3, requiring prolonged renal replacement therapy. This highlights the importance of considering arboviral infections in patients presenting with unexplained shock and cytopenia during transmission seasons.
brief.objective: To report a severe case of West Nile virus infection with septic shock and AKI leading to CKD, emphasizing the need for clinicians to consider WNV in patients with unexplained shock and cytopenia during transmission seasons.
brief.timeline_geography: September 2025, Bouches-du-Rhône department, southern France; possible exposure in Catalonia region, Spain
brief.population_sample: A 63-year-old man with a history of noninsulin-dependent type 2 diabetes mellitus, previous pulmonary embolism, and coronary artery disease with stent placement. He was not immunosuppressed.
brief.key_methods: Polymerase chain reaction (PCR), serology for leptospirosis
key_findings: WNV infection leading to septic shock and AKI requiring renal replacement therapy
Delayed PCR positivity in urine and IgG seroconversion on day 84 post-symptom onset
brief.discussion: This case highlights that WNV infection without early neurological manifestations can lead to severe multiorgan failure, similar to bacterial sepsis. Clinicians should consider WNV in patients with unexplained shock and cytopenia during transmission seasons.

brief.summary: This paper describes a case of immune checkpoint inhibitor-induced encephalitis in a patient with endometrial carcinoma, highlighting diagnostic challenges and the importance of maintaining a high degree of clinical suspicion.
brief.objective: To describe a rare but clinically significant adverse event associated with the use of pembrolizumab in patients with gynecologic cancers.
brief.timeline_geography: 15 days after initiation of pembrolizumab-based therapy, United States ( implied by journal)
brief.population_sample: 68-year-old woman with stage IIIC1 endometrioid endometrial carcinoma
brief.key_methods: Pembrolizumab-based therapy, high-dose intravenous methylprednisolone
key_findings: Pembrolizumab-induced encephalitis may closely mimic an infectious or metabolic etiology.
Rapid neurologic improvement with corticosteroids supported an ICI-related encephalitic process.
brief.discussion: The case highlights diagnostic complexity of pembrolizumab-associated encephalitis in the presence of concurrent infectious and endocrine abnormalities, underlining the importance of early recognition and maintaining a high index of suspicion.

brief.summary: Convalescent individuals who contracted West Nile disease produce antibodies that can protect against the virus and its related orthoflaviviruses, including some types that are tick-borne or mosquito-borne. Human monoclonal antibody W010 was identified as a particularly effective neutralizer of West Nile virus in laboratory experiments, providing complete protection when administered even five days after infection.
brief.objective: To identify antiviral antibodies produced by individuals who have recovered from West Nile disease and to assess the potential protective value of these antibodies against future infections with related viruses.
brief.population_sample: 72 study participants (half males, average age 64.7) with suspected West Nile disease or meningitis who were hospitalized and had high serum neutralizing activity against WNV.
brief.key_methods: ELISA for detecting IgG antibodies targeting the EDIII protein of WNV, a multiplexed bead-based assay to measure IgG autoantibodies binding to IFN-α2 or IFN-ω, RT-PCR for sequencing antibody heavy and light chain gene pairs from individually purified memory B cells.
key_findings: W010 is a human monoclonal antibody that effectively neutralizes West Nile virus and its related orthoflaviviruses
The presence of autoantibodies against IFN-α and/or IFN-ω did not adversely impact the serologic response to WNV
Convalescent individuals who contracted West Nile disease produce antibodies that can protect against the virus and its related orthoflaviviruses
brief.discussion: Results suggest that human monoclonal antibodies, particularly W010, may offer a novel approach to preventing or treating West Nile virus infections. The authors note that these findings could have significant implications for public health strategies, especially in regions where the virus is endemic.
brief.limitations: The study sample size was relatively small (72 participants), and replication of these results with larger cohorts and different populations would be needed to confirm these findings.
brief.recommendations: Future studies should investigate the use of human monoclonal antibodies like W010 for post-exposure prophylaxis against West Nile virus infections, especially in individuals who are immunocompromised or have impaired interferon-I (IFN-I) signaling.

brief.summary: This study investigates the spatial determinants of West Nile virus (WNV) disease incidence in humans across Europe. The research identified key environmental and socio-economic factors that contribute to the spread of WNV, including land cover, climate, and population density.
brief.objective: To investigate the spatial role of land cover on WNV disease incidence in Europe and identify the key factors that contribute to its spread.
brief.study_type: Spatial analysis using geographically weighted regression (GWR) models
brief.timeline_geography: 2005-2019, continental Europe
brief.population_sample: 7,909 human cases with known province of infection
brief.key_methods: Geographically weighted regression (GWR) modeling, Ordinary Least Squares (OLS) analysis
key_findings: Shrubland cover was positively associated with WNV disease incidence across central and eastern Europe.
Mean summer temperature showed a pronounced positive relationship between warmer summer conditions and transmission risk.
Urban cover tended to show slightly positive coefficients in parts of Central Europe but negative associations in southern regions.

brief.summary: WNV NS3 stimulates RNA ATPase activity but struggles to unwind duplex RNA.
brief.objective: To determine if WNV NS3 exhibits RNA-dependent ATPase activity and its ability to unwind duplex RNA.
brief.timeline_geography: Not specified, presumably laboratory experiments.
brief.population_sample: Not specified, in vitro experiments.
brief.key_methods: Fluorescence polarization assays, TLC (thin layer chromatography), native PAGE (polyacrylamide gel electrophoresis).
key_findings: WNV NS3 exhibits RNA-dependent ATPase activity and is stimulated by dsRNA.
WNV NS3 fails to unwind duplex RNA under conditions optimized for HCV NS3.
Reducing reaction temperature or using lower concentrations of ATP and MgCl2 allows WNV NS3 to unwind duplex RNA.
brief.discussion: The study suggests a conserved allosteric activation mechanism among Orthoflavivirus NS3 and other SF2 helicases. The results have implications for the development of therapeutic strategies against flaviviruses.
brief.limitations: The study assumes that HCV NS3 and WNV NS3 exhibit similar biochemical properties, despite differences in enzyme specificity.
brief.recommendations: Further research is needed to understand the enzymatic properties of WNV NS3 and to develop more effective antiviral therapies.

brief.summary: This study reports the genomic epidemiology and phylogeographic reconstruction of West Nile virus 2 in Italy from 2011 to 2023, analyzing 334 whole genome sequences, including newly characterized and previously sequenced data.
brief.objective: To investigate the genetic diversity, spread, and transmission patterns of WNV-2 in Italy over a 12-year period, informing public health strategies for viral surveillance and control.
brief.timeline_geography: Italy, between 2011 and 2023
brief.population_sample: 334 whole genome sequences, with majority (226) from Italian samples, including birds and mosquitoes.
brief.key_methods: Whole-genome sequencing, Illumina DNA Prep and IDT ILMN DNA/RNA Index kit, paired-end sequencing protocol, Geneious Prime software v. 11.1 for consensus sequence generation
key_findings: WNV-2 genetic diversity in Italy
Phylogeographic reconstruction of WNV-2 spread across Europe
Transmission patterns and potential sources of infection
brief.discussion: The study's results highlight the need for continued surveillance and monitoring of WNV-2 in Italy, as well as the importance of understanding its transmission dynamics to inform public health actions.
brief.limitations: Limited temporal resolution in some areas due to collection date gaps
brief.recommendations: Enhanced genomic surveillance and data sharing across European countries to improve understanding and preparedness for virus spread

brief.summary: A study on West Nile Virus (WNV) outbreaks in Andalusia, Spain, documents the coexistence of imported and endemic viruses.
brief.objective: To provide a detailed molecular characterization of the 2024 WNV outbreak in Andalusia and document the coexistence of imported viruses along with endemic viruses.
brief.timeline_geography: Andalusia, Spain, between 2010 and 2024
brief.population_sample: Humans (106 confirmed cases), horses, birds, and mosquitoes
brief.key_methods: Genomic surveillance, phylogenetic analysis, reverse transcription PCR, multiplex PCR, and sequencing on the Illumina iSeq 100 System.
key_findings: The 2024 outbreak marked a resurgence in WNV infections in Andalusia, resulting in 106 confirmed human cases and 16 fatalities
brief.discussion: The study highlights the key role of Spain in the traffic of WNV between Europe and Africa, based on phylogenetic analysis. The results demonstrate the coexistence of imported and endemic viruses during the outbreak.
brief.limitations: None mentioned
brief.recommendations: Implementation of enhanced surveillance measures and vector control strategies to prevent future outbreaks

brief.summary: A mathematical model was developed to study the spread of West Nile virus (WNV) in Germany. The results showed that migratory birds play a crucial role in shaping WNV spreading patterns, and that their mobility can facilitate long-distance transmission of the virus.
brief.objective: To understand the drivers of WNV spread in Germany and to infer estimates of spreading speeds using a temperature-driven PDE model with advection and diffusion processes.
brief.population_sample: Avian hosts, including migratory birds
brief.key_methods: PDE model with advection and diffusion processes, temperature-driven spread of WNV
key_findings: Migratory birds facilitate long-distance transmission of WNV.
The basic reproductive number (R0(x)) identifies low-high risk regions of public health interest, which agreed with the observed WNV cases in birds and equids.
The model detected 2023, 2024, and 2025 cases as early as in 2022 when migratory birds receive more bites.
brief.discussion: Understanding the WNV spreading pattern allows early detection of WNV outbreaks. Identifying high-circulation areas supports early planning and resource allocation for preventive measures.
brief.limitations: Our approach relies on a temperature-driven model, which may not capture other factors that influence WNV spread (e.g., vector control measures). Regional differences in surveillance intensity and reporting may affect the accuracy of our results near national boundaries.
brief.recommendations: Implement systematic surveillance programs to understand the spread of WNV. Effective prevention efforts of WNV may also be implemented at key stopover sites, where migratory birds are likely to rest and interact with local mosquitoes.

brief.summary: This study examines the circulation and overwintering of Usutu virus (USUV) lineages in north-eastern Spain using a One Health perspective, confirming USUV circulation in Catalonia during 2022, 2024, and 2025.
brief.objective: The authors aim to investigate the presence and distribution of USUV strains in wild birds, sentinel chickens, backyard poultry, and mosquitoes in Catalonia between 2021 and 2025.
brief.timeline_geography: Catalonia (north-eastern Spain), within Europe. Sampling performed in different municipalities and provinces over three mosquito activity seasons: May to December (2024) for sentinel chickens, April to November (2024-25) for wild birds, 2025 for backyard poultry, and during routine surveillance from 2021 through 2025 (excluding 2023).
brief.population_sample: Wild birds (369), including residents blackbirds; sentinel chickens (34 serum samples); backyard poultry (70) sampled at slaughterhouse in areas with previous flavivirus circulation. Also, mosquitoes collected through mosquito traps operated throughout the monitoring program.
brief.key_methods: RT-qPCR for molecular detection of USUV RNA, serological analyses using competitive enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay and plaque serum neutralization test to confirm positive samples, viral isolation and sequencing by whole-genome analysis including multiple sequence alignment, phylogenetic analysis conducted in MEGA v12. Immunohistochemical detection of USUV antigen.
key_findings: USUV RNA detected in brain samples of 6 out of 369 wild bird samples collected between 2021 and 2025, highlighting the occurrence of USUV circulation in Catalonia during 2022, 2024, and 2025
brief.discussion: Previous studies had documented USUV infections in European birds, but not within the studied region. Positive detection occurred mainly in early August to late September with a range of Ct values from 17.36 to 33.21. The results show viral presence was significant and widespread, reinforcing evidence for ongoing circulation within Catalonia. All detected blackbirds had higher USUV titres in feathers than any other tissue tested showing consistent result across all examined tissues.
brief.limitations: None mentioned.

brief.summary: This paper evaluates a temperature-dependent reproduction number model (R0rel) as an indicator of West Nile virus transmission in Europe. Results show that despite similar temperature conditions, regions differ in reported cases and years with no cases abound, leading the authors to conclude that R0rel may not provide informative signal on the relationship between temperature and WNV transmission intensity.
brief.objective: To investigate whether a thermal biology-informed reproduction number model (R0rel) can explain patterns of West Nile virus incidence in Europe
brief.timeline_geography: Europe 2010-2023
brief.population_sample: human West Nile virus cases reported by EU/EEA member states
brief.key_methods: temperature data from ERA5-Land dataset, R0rel model based on lab-based mosquito-pathogen trait data
key_findings: Many regions with similar temperature conditions differed in whether they reported WNND cases or not
R0rel calculations may not provide informative signal on the relationship between temperature and WNV transmission intensity
brief.discussion: The study's findings suggest that R0rel may have limitations as an indicator of WNV transmission, highlighting the need for further research into other factors influencing transmission.
brief.limitations: The study notes potential biases in case reporting and surveillance systems
brief.recommendations: Future studies could explore alternative indicators or approaches to understanding WNV transmission and explore how to improve surveillance and reporting systems

brief.summary: The present study detected horses exposed to West Nile Virus (WNV) in Denmark for the first time. These findings indicate that antibody detection in horses may serve as an early warning sign for human exposure to WNV, underscoring the importance of active surveillance and prevention measures in southern areas of Denmark, especially considering the virus's expansion into Europe.
brief.objective: This study aimed to investigate whether horses could serve as sentinel species for detecting WNV circulation in a given country or region, through serological monitoring using multiple assays.
brief.timeline_geography: The findings of this study were based on data collected from the southern parts of Denmark between 2025 and 2026. The study specifically noted that all four horses with WNV-specific antibodies originated from these regions, corresponding well to the observed south-north expansion of WNV in Europe, where a detection in a dead bird in Estonia represents the most northern case registered so far.
brief.population_sample: A total of [number] horses from various clinics across southern Denmark were included in this study, although it should be noted that not all veterinary practitioners who were contacted participated, resulting in an unevenly distributed sampling with fewer clinics being included from the northern part of Denmark. This could potentially introduce some bias when interpreting the seroprevalence rates reported.
brief.key_methods: Serological diagnostics using multiple assays (INgezim West Nile COMPAC ELISA, ID Screen Flavivirus Competition ELISA) to detect WNV antibodies in horse serum samples
key_findings: 50% of horses tested positive for neutralizing antibodies against WNV despite being vaccinated.
Four horses were identified with no related vaccine or travel history originating from the southern parts of Denmark.
There was a clear geographical distribution of WNV-positive cases in these regions, emphasizing the importance of prioritizing surveillance and prevention measures to prevent human exposure.
brief.discussion: These results indicate that antibody detection in horses may be an early warning sign for WNV circulation. The study's findings also suggest that active surveillance and prevention measures should focus on southern areas of Denmark.
brief.limitations: The study had a limitation due to the unevenly distributed sampling, with fewer clinics from the northern part of Denmark participating. Additionally, the sera samples were not analyzed for neutralizing antibodies against other orthoflaviviruses that may co-circulate in these regions, which could potentially cross-react with TBEV antibodies.
brief.recommendations: The authors recommend prioritizing active surveillance and prevention measures to prevent human exposure to WNV, especially focusing on southern areas of Denmark where  WNV appears to be expanding. They also suggest using horses as a potential sentinel species for detecting novel risk areas of both TBEV and WNV.

brief.summary: Physician knowledge and risk perceptions regarding mosquito-borne arboviral diseases were inadequate in Baden-Wuerttemberg, Germany, with only 42% of physicians agreeing to order arboviral testing in a clinical vignette.
brief.objective: To assess the knowledge, risk perceptions, and practices (KPP) of physicians in Baden-Wuerttemberg, Germany regarding mosquito-borne arboviral diseases and their transmission routes.
brief.timeline_geography: May to October 2024, Baden-Wuerttemberg, Germany
brief.population_sample: 473 physicians (response rate of ∼6%) who are general practitioners, internists, or pediatricians registered with the Association of Statutory Health Insurance Physicians of Baden-Wuerttemberg (KVBW)
brief.key_methods: A 44-item questionnaire was used to assess KPP. Descriptive statistics were computed and composite domain scores were calculated and normalized (0-100 scale). Associations between domains and predictors were examined using non-parametric tests, Spearman correlation, and beta regression models.
key_findings: The median normalized knowledge scores were 68.6 (IQR 55.4-79.7), perception scores were 33.3 (26.7-46.7)
A majority of respondents, 75.8% (N = 354) reported only partial knowledge on arboviral transmission routes.
Only 42% would order arboviral testing in a clinical vignette.
brief.limitations: The questionnaire was exploratory and not designed as a psychometrically validated scale. No formal validation procedures were performed.

brief.summary: Flaviviruses, such as Dengue, Zika, and West Nile virus, interact closely with host cell membranes at every stage of their life cycle, relying on specific lipids and lipid-remodeling proteins, presenting potential therapeutic opportunities.
brief.objective: To clarify flavivirus lipid requirements and functions in the viral life cycle
brief.population_sample: Mosquito cells
brief.key_methods: Cryo-electron tomography (cryo-ET) visualization, mass spectrometry-based lipidomics, functionalized lipid probes
key_findings: Host lipids are becoming increasingly apparent in flavivirus pathogenesis
Lipid metabolic enzymes are indispensable for flavivirus replication

brief.summary: This study revisits usambarensine, a bis-indole alkaloid from Strychnos usambarensis, as an antiviral agent with potential to combat COVID-19 viruses.
brief.objective: To explore the antiviral properties of usambarensine against SARS-CoV-2 and other viruses through in vitro assays。
brief.timeline_geography: Root bark extracted from S. usambarensis, collected in 1988 in the Luki region (Republic of the Congo), at the University of Liège (Belgium)
brief.population_sample: Vero E6 cells, zebrafish embryos
brief.key_methods: Flash chromatography, RT-qPCR, HPLC-UV, MS/MS, NMR spectroscopy
key_findings: Usambarensine inhibited SARS-CoV-2 replication by up to 95% in Vero E6 cells.
Zebrafish embryos exposed to usambarensine showed no significant signs of toxicity or developmental abnormalities.
brief.discussion: The study indicates the potential of usambarensine as an antiviral agent. Further investigation is necessary to fully understand its mechanism and efficacy against various viruses.
brief.limitations: Limited cell culture models, variable in vitro conditions
brief.recommendations: Future research could focus on evaluating usambarensine's effectiveness in human clinical trials.

brief.summary: This study explores the target specificity of five flavivirus proteases using protein large language models and proteomic identification methods, revealing a high degree of promiscuity among these enzymes.
brief.objective: To investigate the subsite specificities of Yellow Fever, West Nile Virus, Zika virus, Usutu Virus, and Rocio Virus proteases to inform understanding of their molecular mechanisms in flaviviral replication.
brief.population_sample: murine melanoma cells (B16F10 cell line) and E. coli BL21­(DE3)
brief.key_methods: PICS protocol with Glu-C peptide libraries and protein large language models for predictive modeling
key_findings: A high degree of promiscuity among flaviviral proteases was observed.
The most common amino acid found at the P1 position was Arginine, ranging from 35% in UVP to 60% in WNP.

brief.summary: A study improved an existing model to simulate mosquito behavior traits and predict West Nile Virus transmission, showing that fine-tuning models to specific mosquito species can lead to more accurate predictions.
brief.objective: To develop a mechanistic approach to predict West Nile Virus transmission by adapting an existing R-language package (Mosquito-borne Viral Suitability Estimator) to model Culex pipiens mosquito traits and behavior
brief.study_type: Retrospective cohort study with a customized simulation model
brief.timeline_geography: The study updated the existing model to reflect data from various locations in the United States.
brief.population_sample: Culex pipiens mosquitoes, one of the most common vectors for West Nile Virus (WNV)
brief.key_methods: The authors reformulated equations for mortality, biting rate, and incubation period using Vapor Pressure Deficit (VPD) instead of Relative Humidity to better approximate dehydration stress on mosquitos.
key_findings: Incorporating trait sensitivity to temperature and VPD resulted in species-specific models that may be effective in informing WNV disease prevention efforts
The correlation between MVSE performance (Spearman's rho for WNND incidence and our custom Index P) and probability of Culex pipiens presence was 0.48 (p = 0.03)
Custom-model results were most apparent at the county-annual scale, but model performance was best at the state-monthly scale
brief.discussion: The authors interpret that incorporating specific traits of local mosquito species can lead to more accurate predictions and inform public health officials for better WNV disease prevention efforts
brief.limitations: None mentioned in the article
brief.recommendations: Tuning models to specific mosquito species may be effective in informing WNV disease prevention efforts

brief.summary: This study investigates how environmental conditions affect insecticide resistance in 2 species of Culex mosquitoes (Cx. pipiens and Cx. restuans).
brief.objective: To evaluate the effects of larval diet on adult susceptibility to permethrin resistance in Cx. pipiens and Cx. restuans using a full-sibling design, providing insights into genotype-environment interactions.
brief.timeline_geography: Collected egg rafts from Illinois (IL) locations, experiments performed in August 2022 for Cx. pipiens and summer 2021 for Cx. restuans, data analysis completed before the stated journal year, which is 2026.
brief.population_sample: Cx. pipiens: 20 cages of mosquitoes; Cx. restuans: 28 families, ranging from 62 to 123 larvae per family.
brief.key_methods: Modified CDC bottle bioassays using modified conditions for permethrin resistance testing; mosquito rearing and feeding under controlled environmental conditions.
key_findings: Cx. pipiens: High food treatment increased susceptibility to permethrin, while low food treatment decreased it compared to standard colony conditions.; Cx. restuans: Resistance levels were similar across all 3 diet treatments, with a proportion of mosquitoes surviving the diagnostic dose (43 mg/L).
brief.limitations: This study did not investigate genetic factors contributing to resistance; potential issues with laboratory-reared mosquito populations and variations in natural field conditions.

brief.summary: The article reports on the Western Nile virus (WNV) mosquito surveillance carried out from June to September 2023 and 2024. In 2023, WNV infection was high in mosquitoes, with 4.8% of mosquito pools testing positive. The highest minimum infection rates (MIRs) were observed at C (20.77%) and RA (14.60%). In contrast, MIRs were low at N especially in August (2.58%). Compared to the previous year, WNV infection rates were significantly lower in 2024, with only a total of 25 WNV-positive mosquito pools identified across all sites.
brief.objective: To investigate WNV activity in mosquitoes collected from various sites in 2023 and 2024.
brief.timeline_geography: Study was conducted over two years: 2023, 2024. The geographical location of the study is not specified.
brief.population_sample: Mosquito pools were collected from various sites in 2023 and 2024.
brief.key_methods: Minipools were processed for real-time PCR to detect WNV RNA. A total of 1739 minipools collected across the sampling period were processed, and a proportion of mosquitoes analyzed by real-time PCR revealed that all infected mosquito pools were from Culex species.
key_findings: $2023: Infection rates peaked in August for several sites except N$.
$2024: WNV infection rates were significantly lower compared to the previous year$.
$Only a total of 25 WNV-positive mosquito pools identified across all sites$
analysis_scope_and_conclusion
brief.discussion: The study concludes that, following significant WNV activity in mosquitoes in 2023, the incidence of the disease was unexpectedly low in 2024.

brief.summary: A gene drive system has been engineered to suppress the population of Culex quinquefasciatus mosquitoes, a vector of diseases such as West Nile virus. The system targets the doublesex (dsx) locus and aims to maintain fertility in drive-carrying males while converting genetic females into sterile intersexes.
brief.objective: To design an efficient gene drive system that suppresses population growth of Culex quinquefasciatus mosquitoes, a major vector for several human diseases.
brief.timeline_geography: 2026; not specified by geographic region
brief.population_sample: Culex quinquefasciatus mosquitoes (vector species); approximately 500 eggs microinjected with the gene drive plasmid per experiment
brief.key_methods: CRISPR-based RIDD suppression system, homing-based mechanism targeting exon 4 of the doublesex (dsx) gene, nanos promoter driving Cas9 expression, dual-gRNA configuration with closely spaced and oppositely oriented gRNAs targeting exon 4; microinjection with a plasmid containing both Cas9 and gRNA expression cassettes
key_findings: The designed RIDD construct is capable of precise integration at the dsx locus in Culex quinquefasciatus mosquitoes.

Super-Mendelian inheritance was observed in the M-linked homing-based RIDD construct, with predominant transmission through the male lineage and efficient conversion of genetic females into sterile intersexes.
brief.discussion: The authors discuss how their gene drive system can be applied to control populations of Culex quinquefasciatus mosquitoes. They highlight that this system has the potential to reduce disease spread and improve public health.
brief.limitations: Not mentioned
brief.recommendations: That future studies validate the performance of the designed gene drive system in real-world settings, and assess its stability across generations.

brief.summary: The study finds that West Nile Virus (WNV) seropositivity was higher in areas located in the south than those in the north, with 33.7% of individuals in the south showing seroposivity compared to 8.4% in the north. The age group, region, and residence type were found to be significant risk factors for WNV infection, with adjusted odds ratios increasing with each age group from 2.2 among those aged 10–29 years to 6.5 among those aged 65 years or more.
brief.objective: To investigate the patterns of emergence and circulation of West Nile Virus in Algeria, focusing on seropositivity rates and risk factors associated with WNV infection
brief.timeline_geography: 2017-2018, five provinces in Algeria
brief.population_sample: 1235 leftover serum samples
brief.key_methods: ELISA (Enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay), PRNT90 (Plaque Reduction Neutralization Test 90%), PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction)
key_findings: West Nile Virus seropositivity was higher in areas located in the south than those in the north
Age group, region, and residence type were significant risk factors for WNV infection
brief.discussion: The study highlights the need to consider regional variations in WNV prevalence when developing public health strategies.
brief.limitations: Only 6.5% of suspected WNND cases were confirmed, which may be due to the limitations of serological testing.
brief.recommendations: Further studies are needed to investigate the underlying causes of WNV circulation and to develop targeted interventions for regions with high seropositivity rates.

brief.summary: This study examines mosquito feeding behavior and its implications for transmission of West Nile virus (WNV) and Rift Valley fever virus (RVFV) in Madagascar. A nationwide survey over two years revealed that mosquitoes resting inside houses were more likely to feed on animals than on humans.
brief.objective: To investigate factors influencing the blood feeding behavior of mosquito vectors of WNV and RVFV in a national survey across six climatic zones of Madagascar over two years.
brief.timeline_geography: Madagascar, February 2019-December 2019
brief.population_sample: 25 villages located in 24 districts distributed across the entire country with 25 study sites
brief.key_methods: Endophilic engorged mosquitoes were collected indoor using commercial insecticide aerosol sprays and exophilic engorged mosquitoes using improved Muirhead-Thomson pit traps.
key_findings: Mosquitoes resting inside houses were mostly feeding on animals (cattle, pigs, sheep/goats) rather than humans.
Highest frequency of animal blood meal was found from cattle.

brief.summary: A data-parsimonious model predicts West Nile virus spillover in Orange, Los Angeles, and Riverside counties.
brief.objective: The authors developed a model to predict the timing of spillover onset of West Nile virus using historical data from 2006-2024.
brief.timeline_geography: 2006-2024, Orange County, Los Angeles, and Riverside counties, California
brief.population_sample: Historical data from 15 years in three US counties
brief.key_methods: Data-parsimonious model, leave-one-year-out cross-validation, retrospective forecasting approach
key_findings: The model predicted spillover onset intervals within the actual time in 73% of cases for Orange County and 58% for Los Angeles County.
The accuracy of predictions improved with increasing confidence levels, but showed little improvement beyond 95% confidence.
brief.discussion: The authors' results suggest that a data-parsimonious model can effectively predict West Nile virus spillover in targeted regions, using a range of confidence levels to optimize accuracy. This approach could have practical applications for public health officials.
brief.limitations: The study's reliance on historical data and the limited scope of the three-county analysis may restrict generalizability to other areas and climates.
brief.recommendations: Public health officials in targeted regions can use this model to anticipate and prepare for West Nile virus spillover. The study also suggests that more widespread application of machine learning techniques could provide valuable insights for public health decision-making.

brief.summary: This study reveals host feeding patterns of Aedes aegypti and Culex quinquefasciatus mosquitoes using bloodmeal metabarcoding in Guatemala and Texas, USA.
brief.objective: The objective was to characterize natural host-feeding patterns by identifying blood-fed females from rural Guatemala and south Texas, USA, and examining how housing infrastructure may influence mosquito access to indoor environments.
brief.timeline_geography: rural Guatemala and south Texas, USA (2022 rainy season)
brief.population_sample: 243 blood-fed female mosquitoes collected from 77 households in Guatemala and 121 blood-fed Ae. aegypti examined in south Texas
brief.key_methods: bloodmeal metabarcoding, household surveys to characterize housing features
key_findings: In Guatemala, Cx. quinquefasciatus exhibited higher rates of mixed feeding than Ae. aegypti (64.7% vs. 19.5%).
Ae. aegypti in south Texas showed the highest mixed feeding rate at 85.3%, significantly greater than Guatemala Ae. aegypti.
Humans were detected in 37/41 (90.2%) of the Ae. aegypti bloodmeals, chickens in 10/41 (24.4%), and Turdus sp. in 2/41 (4.9%).
Forage-ratio inference indicated over-utilization of humans relative to availability.
Dogs were detected in 60/68 (88.2%) of bloodmeals in south Texas, and their utilization was significantly over-utilized.
brief.discussion: Mixed feeding patterns differed significantly between mosquito species within Guatemala, and study sites exhibited substantial differences in housing infrastructure.
brief.limitations: None mentioned
brief.recommendations: The findings support the use of bloodmeal metabarcoding as a tool for investigating host-feeding patterns. Household surveys can aid in understanding how housing features may influence mosquito access to indoor environments.

brief.summary: Scientists developed a modeling approach to control West Nile virus in Germany by incorporating vertical transmission into their models, which showed that including this factor can help predict and prevent outbreaks.
brief.objective: The objective of this study was to investigate the impact of vertical transmission on West Nile virus (WNV) transmission risk in Germany, using a mechanistic epidemic model.
brief.study_type: This paper uses a mechanistic epidemiological modeling approach to simulate WNV transmission risk across Germany.
brief.timeline_geography: Germany, between 2018 and 2023
brief.population_sample: Mosquitoes (infection rates) and birds (case data from FLI37)
brief.key_methods: A mechanistic epidemic model for two scenarios: one with vertical transmission (WNV-VT model) and the other without (WNV model); Receiver Operating Characteristics (ROC) curves to evaluate model performance
key_findings: Incorporating vertical transmission into WNV models can help predict and prevent outbreaks in Germany.
Vertical transmission impact rates above 0.5 identify locations where WNV has become endemic.
Mosquito control strategies, including mechanical, biological, and chemical control, can reduce WNV transmission risk by up to 34%.
brief.discussion: The simulated risk maps from the WNV-VT model were compared with daily WNV infection notification data in birds from the TSIS platform, showing good agreement between modeled predictions and observed cases.
brief.limitations: The authors acknowledge that their study was limited to a specific region (Germany) and that further research is needed to understand the broader impacts of vertical transmission on WNV transmission risk worldwide.
brief.recommendations: The study recommends incorporating vertical transmission into epidemiological models for other mosquito-borne diseases as well, and using this approach to predict and prevent outbreaks.

brief.summary: This study examines the efficacy of honey bee venom and its nanoemulsion in inhibiting West Nile virus (WNV) replication in Vero cells.
brief.objective: To investigate the antiviral properties of crude honey bee venom and its nanoemulsion against WNV, in vitro
brief.timeline_geography: Egypt
brief.population_sample: Vero cell line from African green monkey
brief.key_methods: Cytotoxicity assay using MTT (3-(4,5-dimethylthiazol-2-yl)-2,5-diphenyltetrazolium bromide) to measure cell viability and IC50 calculation.
key_findings: Crude honey bee venom exhibits antiviral activity against WNV with an IC50 value of 9.65 ± 1.23 μg/mL
The nanoemulsion bee venom formulation shows greater efficacy in reducing virus titers compared to crude bee venom at lower cytotoxic concentrations
brief.discussion: The results suggest that both formulations possess antiviral properties, but the nanoemulsion formulation appears more effective due to its improved solubility and stability.
brief.limitations: Experimentally defined non-cytotoxic concentrations used for each formulation.

brief.summary: A key takeaway from this paper is that the minimum infectious dose of West Nile virus (WNV) differs by lineage 1 and 2, with a lower threshold observed in Culex species.
brief.objective: The authors investigate differences in the transmission potential and behavior of WNV lineages 1 and 2 using a laboratory experiment.
brief.timeline_geography: incubated for 14 days at 24 ± 5 °C
brief.population_sample: three mosquito species: Culex pipiens biotype pipiens, Culex torrentium, and Aedes albopictus
brief.key_methods: blood meal titers (TCID50/mL), salivation assay, hurdle model analysis of predictors for viral infection and transmission
key_findings: mosquito species affects the minimum infectious dose of WNV lineage 1
a lower threshold is observed in Culex species
WNV-L2 MID was lower compared to WNV-L1
brief.discussion: the authors interpret these findings as supporting a two-component mixture model where lineages L1 and L2 have different transmission potential. This has implications for disease models and risk assessment.
brief.limitations: due to the limited number of field-caught mosquitoes, Culex pipiens biotype pipiens only had samples tested at 105 TCID50/mL for WNV-L1
brief.recommendations: (none explicitly mentioned in the study)

brief.summary: This study identified a distinct epitope on the E dimer protein that is selectively recognized by the WNV-86 antibody, providing insights into the functional properties of this antibody and potential avenues for vaccine development.
brief.objective: The objective of this study was to determine the binding architecture of the WNV-86 Fab on the virion and characterize the epitope recognized by this antibody.
brief.key_methods: cryo-electron microscopy (cryo-EM), Fourier shell correlation (FSC) estimation
key_findings: A distinct E dimer epitope underlies selective recognition by a protective human West Nile virus antibody.
The WNV-86 Fab binds to two of the three potential binding sites in the asymmetric subunit, with preferential binding at the general dimer position.

brief.summary: This study examines how West Nile virus's E-protein interacts with graphene and phosphorene nanomaterials at the molecular level using computational methods.
brief.objective: To investigate the protein-surface van der Waals interactions without edge- or confinement-induced contributions, which is a challenge in earlier reports on confined phosphorene and graphene derivatives.
brief.timeline_geography: not mentioned
brief.population_sample: West Nile virus's E-protein
brief.key_methods: Brownian Dynamics (BD) simulations, Molecular Dynamics (MD) simulations with the OPLS/AA force field applied to both the protein and the surface.
key_findings: The structure of the E-protein was accurately modeled using a flat surface representation as it perceives the phosphorene and graphene surfaces locally.
Van der Waals interactions between the protein and surface were studied without edge- or confinement-induced contributions.
brief.discussion: This study provides new insights into protein-surface interactions, enabling design of nanomaterials for specific applications, such as drug delivery or biological sensing.
brief.limitations: The accuracy of the results relies on the quality of the force field used in the simulations. A limitation is that the confined phosphorene and graphene derivatives were not thoroughly studied.
brief.recommendations: Further experimentation can validate these predictions, potentially opening avenues for new medical applications.

brief.summary: The paper reviews the current state of knowledge on West Nile virus (WNV) epidemiology, prevention, clinical features, diagnosis, treatment, and research gaps. The review highlights the impact of global ecological change on zoonotic diseases, with WNV being one of the most widespread arboviruses worldwide, causing seasonal outbreaks in temperate regions.
brief.objective: The objective of the study was to summarize current knowledge on WNV epidemiology, pathogenesis, clinical spectrum, diagnostic challenges, therapeutic options, prevention, and research gaps, highlighting the impact of global ecological change on zoonotic diseases.
brief.timeline_geography: Temporally: 1937-2024; Geographically: globally, with a focus on Europe, USA, Africa, and the Middle East.
brief.population_sample: Humans, birds (primarily passeriformes), horses, mosquitoes (Culex spp.), other mammals such as squirrels, rabbits, racoons, bats.
brief.key_methods: Integrated vector control, veterinary surveillance, donor screening, development of experimental antivirals, monoclonal antibodies, and interferon for treatment, refinement of diagnostic tests.
key_findings: WNV is one of the most widespread arboviruses worldwide
Neuroinvasive disease causes severe morbidity and long-term sequelae
Integrated One Health surveillance, improved diagnostics, and development of effective vaccines and antivirals are crucial to mitigate future outbreaks.
brief.discussion: The review concludes that WNV exemplifies the impact of global ecological change on zoonotic diseases. Strengthening surveillance, refining diagnostics, and advancing antivirals and vaccines through multidisciplinary collaboration are essential to mitigate future outbreaks.
brief.limitations: No specific antiviral therapy exists; management is supportive; few licensed human vaccines are available.
brief.recommendations: Strengthening integrated One Health surveillance, refinement of diagnostic tests, development of experimental antivirals, monoclonal antibodies, and interferon, advancement of effective vaccines through multidisciplinary collaboration.

brief.summary: This review synthesizes current findings on the role of TRP channels in the pathogenesis of Flaviviridae viruses, highlighting their potential as targets for host-directed antiviral therapies.
brief.objective: The aim of this comprehensive review is to establish a conceptual framework for understanding TRP channel biology in Flaviviridae infection and guide future research on antiviral strategies.
brief.timeline_geography: global
brief.population_sample: hundreds of millions of individuals across more than 100 countries and regions affected by Flaviviridae viruses.
brief.key_methods: the strategic manipulation of host cellular signaling to support viral entry, replication, assembly, and release, particularly the disruption of intracellular calcium (Ca2+) homeostasis
key_findings: TRP channels are critical mediators of viral infection, functioning as “molecular gatekeepers” that pathogens co-opt or disrupt to promote their replication and spread.
Pharmacological inhibition of TRP channels has been shown to reduce Flavivirus infection and dissemination.
brief.discussion: Despite effective vaccines existing for some Flaviviruses, outbreaks continue to emerge due to globalization and urbanization. Therefore, a comprehensive understanding of the biological characteristics of Flaviviruses is urgently needed.
brief.limitations: A systematic analysis of the role and mechanisms of TRP channels across Flaviviridae infection remains lacking
brief.recommendations: Future research should aim to develop novel antiviral strategies targeting TRP channels for host-directed therapies.

brief.summary: West Nile virus and Usutu virus exhibit different properties in terms of NS1 glycoprotein secretion, stability, and impact on blood-brain barrier.,
brief.objective: The authors aimed to compare the functional and biochemical properties of NS1 from West Nile virus (WNV) and Usutu virus (USUV), and their impact on host immune responses and viral dissemination.
brief.timeline_geography: France, Hungary, Germany with data collection periods not specified in abstract
brief.population_sample: Human patients infected with either WNV or USUV from an unspecified number of countries, as well as laboratory mice.
brief.key_methods: In vitro cell culture using HEK293 cells, in vivo mouse models, RT-qPCR for viral identification, IgM ELISA for antibody detection
key_findings: WNV NS1 is secreted at higher levels, has greater thermal stability, and disrupts blood-brain barrier integrity.
USUV NS1 exhibits lower secretion efficiency, reduced stability, and does not compromise blood-brain barrier integrity.
Induction of distinct transcriptional responses in brain endothelial cells.
Higher serum NS1 levels and stronger systemic inflammation were observed in WNV-infected mice compared to USUV-infected mice.

brief.summary: This study investigates the pharmacokinetics and tissue distribution of favipiravir in preclinical models, aiming to understand how plasma exposure affects antiviral coverage.
brief.objective: To assess how plasma exposure and tissue distribution shape antiviral coverage using a tissue-based PK/PD framework, with the goal of informing evidence-based antiviral repurposing efforts.
brief.timeline_geography: Conducted in Syrian golden hamsters and cynomolgus macaques
brief.population_sample: N/A (in vitro activity), N = 450 laboratory-confirmed cases, n = unknown (no sample size mentioned)
brief.key_methods: LC-MS/MS analysis to quantify favipiravir and its hydroxylated metabolite (M1) in plasma and organs.
key_findings: Favipiravir showed heterogeneous tissue distribution, with highest levels in kidney, gut, and respiratory organs.
Organ exposure ranking was broadly similar across species.
Tissue IQs were often lower than plasma IQs, indicating that plasma monitoring can overestimate target-organ coverage.
brief.discussion: The authors interpret these findings against existing data, suggesting favourable coverage for influenza and RSV, heterogeneous dosage-dependent coverage for chikungunya and other viruses, intermediate coverage for Zika virus, and limited coverage for SARS-CoV-2 and ebolavirus.
brief.limitations: Selection bias, under-reporting, and insufficient margins for some viruses
brief.recommendations: Dose reassessment and safety data are needed to mitigate limitations, and further research is required to optimize favipiravir's antiviral efficacy.

brief.summary: This study examines the spatio-temporal dynamics of Culex pipiens s.l. in Northern Italy, identifying dominant drivers of inter-annual variability and short-term temperature influences on mosquito abundance.
brief.objective: To investigate how environmental variability across multiple temporal and spatial scales affects the populations of Culex pipiens s.l., a primary vector for West Nile virus transmission in Europe.
brief.study_type: Entomological study using nine-year entomological dataset from an extensive monitoring network in Northern Italy
brief.timeline_geography: The study took place over nine years (2014-2022) within the Po Valley region of Northern Italy.
brief.population_sample: A total of 139 trapping sites across rural and urban areas in Lombardy and Emilia-Romagna regions, covering approximately 24,000 km2
brief.key_methods: Modified CDC traps baited with carbon dioxide (CO2–CDC traps) were used to collect mosquitoes fortnightly from June to October.
key_findings: Strong persistence in population states across both years and months, consistently modulated by hydroclimatic conditions
Pre-activity precipitation emerged as a dominant driver of inter-annual variability. Within seasons, short-term temperature exerted a strong, nonlinear influence on Cx. pipiens s.l. abundance.
Spatial analyses identified persistent hotspots associated with irrigated agricultural systems, wetlands, and major river corridors.
brief.discussion: Results show that climatically and environmentally driven indicators can be translated into actionable tools for risk assessment and adaptive vector surveillance within integrated One Health frameworks for WNV.

brief.summary: This systematic review evaluated the effectiveness of natural predators, microbial bioinsecticides, and plant-based bioinsecticides in reducing mosquito-borne disease burden across diverse settings.
brief.objective: The objective of this study was to assess whether environmentally friendly interventions are effective for disease control by evaluating the impact of these biological vector control methods on mosquito-borne diseases such as chikungunya, dengue, Zika virus infection, and malaria.
key_findings: Natural predators, microbial bioinsecticides, and plant-based bioinsecticides reduced disease burden in 16 out of 18 studies compared to control groups.
The most effective interventions were larvivorous fish and copepods for reducing the burden of dengue and malaria.
brief.discussion: These biological vector control methods show potential to reduce the burden of mosquito-borne diseases across diverse settings, supporting their role as promising alternatives or complements for disease control. However, future studies would benefit from more experimental designs, standardized epidemiological outcomes, and robust statistical analysis.

brief.summary: Two ornamental plants, Citronella-Scented Geranium and prostrate rosemary, were tested for their spatial repellency against host-seeking mosquitoes in laboratory and field trials. The results showed that neither plant provided significant repellency under realistic field deployment conditions.
brief.objective: To evaluate the effectiveness of whole ornamental plants as spatial repellents against host-seeking mosquitoes using laboratory Y-tube olfactometer bioassays and replicated field trials in both urban and rural locations.
brief.timeline_geography: California's Central Valley, with field trials conducted in Sacramento from early July through late October
brief.population_sample: Host-seeking mosquitoes (Ae. aegypti females)
brief.key_methods: Y-tube olfactometer bioassays, replicated field trials in both urban and rural locations
key_findings: Neither Citronella-Scented Geranium nor prostrate rosemary provided significant spatial repellency against host-seeking mosquitoes under realistic field deployment conditions.
The metofluthrin-based spatial repellent (Thermacell E90) produced consistently lower mosquito captures at both locations.
brief.discussion: The study suggests that whole ornamental plants do not provide effective spatial repellency against host-seeking mosquitoes. This finding may be relevant for public health officials and residents interested in plant-based mosquito repellents.
brief.limitations: The study acknowledges some limitations, including potential selection bias and under-reporting of mosquito captures. However, the authors note that these factors are unlikely to significantly affect the overall conclusion.
brief.recommendations: Based on the findings, the authors do not recommend using whole ornamental plants as spatial repellents against host-seeking mosquitoes. They suggest exploring other evidence-based methods for controlling mosquito-borne diseases.

brief.summary: This study investigated the emergence, persistence, and intermixing of Usutu virus in the Netherlands through phylodynamic analyses.
brief.objective: The authors aimed to reconstruct the dynamics of Usutu virus emergence and establishment in a non-endemic temperate region using genome sequencing and phylogenetic analysis.
brief.timeline_geography: Netherlands, 2016-2023
brief.population_sample: Birds (Eurasian Blackbirds) and mosquitoes
brief.key_methods: Genome sequencing, Phylodynamic analysis using BEAST package
key_findings: Two predominant Usutu virus clades emerged from lineage Africa 3 in the Netherlands region.
Viral lineages circulation shows a temporal pattern consistent with invasion followed by local persistence.
There is spatial intermixing of viral lineages circulating in the region.
brief.discussion: The study provides insight into the dynamics of emergence and establishment of Usutu virus in a non-endemic temperate region, which may be relevant for understanding re-emergence of related arboviruses such as West Nile virus.
brief.limitations: Selection bias due to sample reporting, and under-reporting or sampling biases were not explored.

brief.summary: A structural element of the West Nile virus genome called SL-I has been found to regulate viral translation by acting as an inhibitor.
brief.objective: To understand the role of the SL-I structural element in regulating viral translation of the West Nile virus.
brief.study_type: Biological study involving molecular biology techniques, specifically in vitro transcription and translation assays.
brief.timeline_geography: No specific timeline or geography is mentioned. The study used Vero cells (derived from African green monkey kidney) for culturing and testing.
brief.population_sample: Viral RNA was derived from the WNV NY99-flamingo382–99 strain (no human subjects involved).
brief.key_methods: RNA constructs were created and tested using in vitro transcription, translation assays, and 40S ribosomal subunit purification. The study also used selective 2′-hydroxyl acylation analysed by primer extension (SHAPE) analyses to detect 40S positioning at the 3' UTR.
key_findings: The SL-I element acts as a translation inhibitor of WNV in a cap-dependent translation context, primarily affecting multi-round translation efficiency.
brief.discussion: The authors interpret these findings as providing new insights into the role of the 3′ UTR SL-I element in translation regulation and suggest that WNV translation is a finely tuned process dependent on multiple partners.

brief.summary: This study developed a novel, subunit nanoparticle vaccine candidate against West Nile virus (WNV) by displaying the envelope protein domain III on a cholera toxin B subunit scaffold. The recombinant antigen showed strong humoral responses with balanced IgG1/IgG2a ratios and neutralizing titres comparable to those elicited by formalin-inactivated WNV, without cross-reactivity with other flaviviruses.
brief.objective: To develop a scalable, safer, and cost-effective subunit nanoparticle vaccine candidate against West Nile virus (WNV), addressing the current lack of an approved human vaccine.
brief.timeline_geography: the study was conducted in laboratory settings with Escherichia coli expression system
brief.population_sample: immunized mice were studied to assess the vaccine efficacy
brief.key_methods: recombinant antigen production, size exclusion chromatography (SEC) analysis, and dynamic light scattering (DLS) analysis
key_findings: The recombinant WNV subunit nanoparticle vaccine showed strong humoral responses in immunized mice with balanced IgG1/IgG2a ratios.
Neutralising titres comparable to those elicited by formalin-inactivated WNV were achieved.
No cross-reactivity was observed with other flaviviruses

brief.summary: Effective mosquito surveillance is crucial to monitoring and preventing the spread of mosquito-borne diseases. This study compared two adult mosquito traps, Biogents BG-Sentinel (BGS) and Mosquito Magnet(r) Executive (MM), on British mosquitoes across four wetlands in south-east England.
brief.objective: To evaluate the relative trapping efficiency of BGS and MM traps on British mosquitoes and to determine which trap is better suited for collecting large sample sizes of mammalophagic species or enzootic vectors such as Culex pipiens.
brief.timeline_geography: Four wetlands in south-east England, over a 12-week period (July-September 2022)
brief.population_sample: 11,584 adult female mosquitoes representing 15 species
brief.key_methods: Two adult mosquito traps: Biogents BG-Sentinel (BGS) and Mosquito Magnet(r) Executive (MM), each trap type with distinct features such as trap design, baiting materials, and operating systems. Box-Gravid trap fitted with an FTA(tm) card for detecting arboviruses.
key_findings: MM trap captured a significantly higher total number of mosquitoes
BGS trap demonstrated greater species evenness and was more effective at catching Culex (Culex) pipiens L., 1758. No evidence of WNV was detected in any mosquito pools or FTA(tm) cards.
brief.discussion: The findings provide evidence-based recommendations for future UK wetland surveillance and enhance preparedness for emerging vector-borne disease risks.
brief.limitations: Spatial variation strongly influenced catch rates, with significant differences between wetlands. Site-specific surveillance in wetland ecosystems is crucial to account for variations in mosquito abundance and species composition.
brief.recommendations: Complementary trap use to optimise sampling of mammalophagic and enzootic mosquito species in UK wetland monitoring programmes.

brief.summary: The study in Eastern Ontario, Canada, reveals mosquito feeding patterns consistent with those observed in other North American regions. The findings highlight pathways of transmission for West Nile and eastern equine encephalitis viruses to human populations.
brief.objective: To identify bloodmeal hosts fed on by mosquitoes using DNA barcoding and investigate if these hosts are representative of the entire host community using species accumulation curves and Chao richness estimates
brief.timeline_geography: 2014-2019, Eastern Ontario, Canada, across urban environments, agricultural cropland, rivers, mixed deciduous and coniferous forests, and some wetlands
brief.population_sample: A total of 292 mosquitoes were analyzed, belonging to six species: Aedes cinereus, Aedes vexans, Coquillettidia perturbans, Culex pipiens/restuans, Ochlerotatus stimulans, and Ochlerotatus trivittatus
brief.key_methods: Mosquitoes were sampled using CDC light traps baited with a UV lamp and 1.9 kg of dry ice at 54 sites across the region from June to September over five years, followed by DNA barcoding analysis of blood-fed mosquitoes to identify bloodmeal hosts
key_findings: Culex species almost exclusively fed on birds

American robins (Turdus migratorius) were observed as amplification hosts for WNV and potential exposure points for humans; Aedes vexans, a potential bridge vector, also showed high-frequency feeding on humans
brief.discussion: Despite the limitations in fully characterizing the bloodmeal host community, the study contributes to a better understanding of mosquito vectors in Eastern North America
brief.limitations: The study's sampling effort was indicated by species accumulation curves and Chao richness estimates to not be fully representative of the entire host community, highlighting the need for further directed sampling efforts

brief.summary: A novel alignment-free computation strategy is presented, enabling the identification of conserved diagnostic targets in highly variable viral genera (e.g., Orthoflavivirus), crucial for developing broad-spectrum molecular diagnostics. This breakthrough provides a powerful tool for frontline clinical diagnosis and global outbreak surveillance.
brief.objective: To develop an inclusive pan-genus molecular diagnostics framework that detects multiple mosquito-borne viruses simultaneously, overcoming traditional methods' limitations in dealing with rapid mutation and high nucleotide divergence.
brief.timeline_geography: no specific geographic location mentioned; 2025-2026 timeframe
brief.population_sample: 11,846 viral RefSeq genomes (representative of Orthoflavivirus genus)
brief.key_methods: [1-k-mer analysis and De Bruijn graphs for alignment-free detection, [2-KITSUNE k selection with ACF for shortest unique k-mers]
key_findings: A conserved 600-bp region in the non-structural protein 5 gene was identified within Orthoflavivirus genus.
The developed TaqMan RT-qPCR assay achieved 97.33% overall accuracy and showed 100% sensitivity and specificity for DENV serotypes in clinical evaluation of archived samples.
brief.discussion: This study validates the alignment-free, k-mer-guided strategy for uncovering conserved diagnostic targets in highly variable viral genera, enabling robust broad frontline surveillance through scalable tool development. The identified assay offers a crucial diagnostic aid for global outbreak preparedness.
brief.limitations: Selection bias and under-reporting limitations implicitly acknowledged by authors based on experimental design and data quality consideration; limitations explicitly mentioned are computational burden of traditional alignment-based approaches
brief.recommendations: The computational framework used in this study is scalable for future pandemic preparedness. This tool provides a generalizable method to uncover conserved diagnostic targets across different viral genera.

brief.summary: A broad neutralization response to multiple flaviviruses is elicited by targeting quaternary epitopes on native flaviviruses, which could inform the design of next-generation pan-flavivirus vaccine strategies.
brief.objective: To understand the basis of quaternary structural epitope recognition and its implications for next-generation pan-flavivirus vaccine strategies
brief.timeline_geography: Global, with a focus on flaviviruses that pose significant global health threats
brief.key_methods: Structural characterization of patient-derived neutralizing antibodies
key_findings: Quaternary epitopes are conserved across multiple flaviviruses and are essential for broad neutralization response.
Flavivirus’s replication cycle starts with cell entry via interaction with multiple types of cell attachment factors or receptors.
Imature virus particles can also potentially become infectious upon interacting with anti-prM antibodies from prior infections.
brief.discussion: The authors discuss mechanistic insights of bnAbs targeting different quaternary epitopes found on pathogenic flaviviruses, and implications for next-generation pan-flavivirus vaccine strategies
brief.limitations: Incomplete maturation process can result in the production of a mixed population comprising completely mature, partially mature, and immature virus particles.
brief.recommendations: Broad protection from multiple flaviviruses using quaternary epitopes-based immunogens is proposed.

brief.summary: This study investigates the formation of aggresome-like structures in human neural progenitor cells and A549 cells infected with West Nile virus or Zika virus. The researchers found that both viruses induce asymmetric clustering of viral replication vesicles, which is a characteristic of aggresome formation.
brief.objective: To understand how different orthoflaviviruses (such as WNV and ZIKV) induce aggresome-like structures in specific cell types, and to investigate the mechanisms behind this phenomenon.
brief.timeline_geography: Infections were conducted in A549 cells or human neural progenitor cells at various time points between 16-40 hours post-infection
brief.population_sample: Human neural progenitor cells and A549 cells
brief.key_methods: Immunofluorescence assay (IFA), Western blotting, Plaque assay.
key_findings: Asymmetric clustering of viral replication vesicles was observed in A549 cells infected with WNV or ZIKV
brief.discussion: The formation of aggresome-like structures delayed activation of cell death pathways and extended virus production. Both cell type-specific and orthoflavivirus-specific characteristics determine whether a particular infection induces aggresome formation.
brief.limitations: The study only investigated two specific types of cells (A549 and human neural progenitor cells) and three different viruses (WNV, ZIKV, and Kun). Other cell types or viruses may exhibit different responses.
brief.recommendations: Further studies should investigate the mechanisms behind aggresome formation in different cell types and viruses. This knowledge could provide new insights into potential treatment strategies for virus infections.

brief.summary: The authors quantified the health and economic burdens of emerging infectious diseases (EIDs) globally, and highlighted that pandemics caused significant historical and projected unweighted and weighted full burdens in the USA and globally. Non-pandemic EIDs, such as dengue and cholera, imposed large historical and projected full burdens globally.
brief.objective: To quantify the health and economic burdens of high-priority EIDs across 223 countries and territories from 2000 to 2022, and project future disease burdens using Monte Carlo simulation.
brief.timeline_geography: Globally, historically from 2000-2022 and prospectively from 2025-2034. Historical projections for the USA, but not US territories.
brief.population_sample: 223 countries and territories including the USA and its US territories, across all symptomatic cases of 15 high-priority EIDs
brief.key_methods: Quantification and ranking method using health burdens (DALY losses), economic burdens (direct and indirect costs during hospitalization) and weighted measures adjusting for global disparities in ability-to-pay. Projection model accounting for pandemics using Monte Carlo simulation.
key_findings: Pandemics caused the largest historical and projected unweighted and weighted full burdens globally.
Non-pandemic EIDs, such as dengue and cholera, imposed large historical and projected full burdens globally.
Weighted full burdens exceeded five times the unweighted ones.
brief.discussion: The study highlights the importance of addressing emerging infectious diseases.
brief.limitations: None explicitly mentioned in the text. Data constraints prevented projecting US territory burdens historically.
brief.recommendations: Control measures to mitigate pandemics and other EIDs are warranted based on these findings.

brief.summary: This case report documents severe Usutu virus encephalitis in an elderly patient treated with corticosteroids.
brief.objective: The goal of this study is to describe a case of severe Usutu virus meningoencephalitis treated with dexamethasone and discuss the potential role of steroids in viral encephalitis.
brief.timeline_geography: 2026, Italy
brief.population_sample: elderly patient
brief.key_methods: dexamethasone treatment
key_findings: Severe Usutu virus meningoencephalitis diagnosed in an elderly patient
Treatment with corticosteroids (dexamethasone) reported
brief.discussion: The study discusses the potential benefits and drawbacks of using steroids in viral encephalitis, citing conflicting case reports on the topic.

brief.summary: A risk assessment model predicts areas in Europe where West Nile fever is likely to occur in equines.
brief.objective: To develop an ecological niche model that identifies potential geographic distribution of WNF occurrence in Europe, by integrating WNF outbreaks with environmental variables and predicting risk areas for the disease.
brief.timeline_geography: Europe, from 2010 to 2023
brief.population_sample: Equines (horses), N = 602 unique outbreak records
brief.key_methods: Time series decomposition using STL model in R, Linear directional mean analysis in ArcGIS, Spatiotemporal clustering analysis using SaTScan v10.1.2, Ecological niche modeling with MaxEnt model and ENMTools software
key_findings: The risk areas for WNF occurrence in Europe are predicted to be along the Danube River and other water bodies.
The probability of WNF occurrence is significantly higher near urban and agricultural areas.
brief.discussion: This study provides a risk map for WNF occurrence in equines across Europe, which can guide veterinary authorities in surveillance and preventive strategies. The findings highlight the importance of considering environmental factors in understanding disease spread.
brief.limitations: The model assumes that historical patterns will continue into the future; however, climate change and other anthropogenic factors may alter these dynamics. Additionally, data quality issues, such as spatial autocorrelation and sampling bias, were not fully addressed during variable selection and modeling.
brief.recommendations: Future studies should investigate the impact of climate change on WNF occurrence patterns and explore potential improvements to the risk assessment model.

brief.summary: A process-based model simulating the life-cycle of Culex pipiens s.s./Cx. torrentium in Germany was developed with a particular focus on depicting realistic overwintering behaviour, including diapause induced through photoperiod and temperature in the larval stage.
brief.objective: The authors aim to improve our understanding of the spatial-temporal occurrence of Cx. pipiens s.s./Cx. torrentium in Germany by developing a process-based model that can simulate realistic overwintering behaviour.
brief.timeline_geography: Germany
brief.population_sample: 106 sampling sites
brief.key_methods: Process-based model, simulation, local temperature and rainfall data
key_findings: A significant association between relative simulated and observed mosquito abundance was found for 75% of the sampling sites.
An overall beta mixed-effects model across all sites was also significant (estimate = 2.17, standard error = 0.062, Z-value = 35.03, p-value < 0.0001).

brief.summary: This study detected West Nile virus in louse flies collected from rehabilitated raptors in South Carolina, with a 42% positivity rate among over 70 fly pools tested.
brief.objective: To investigate the presence of West Nile virus in louse flies attached to rehabilitated raptors in South Carolina as part of a surveillance study.
brief.timeline_geography: August 2023 to December 2024, collected from 18 counties across South Carolina, USA, and one county in Georgia, USA
brief.population_sample: 71 injured raptors representing 14 birds of prey species
brief.key_methods: louse fly collection, real-time polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR) testing for West Nile virus RNA
key_findings: 42% of louse fly pools tested showed West Nile virus RNA-positive
Icosta americana was the most common louse fly species collected with 59 out of 61 identified flies being this species
brief.discussion: These findings suggest that louse flies can act as vectors for West Nile virus transmission, highlighting the importance of considering zoonotic transmission in raptor rehabilitation settings.
