brief.summary: The study found widespread distribution of three viruses including dengue, yellow fever, and West Nile viruses across 18 surveyed prefectures in Guinea. The highest seroprevalence of antibodies was observed in N’Zerekore (43.9% for dengue), Kankan Prefecture (54.7% for yellow fever), and Forecariah (53.0% for West Nile virus). Seropositivity was more frequent among adults and individuals involved in farming or livestock breeding.
brief.objective: The authors aim to investigate the circulation of arboviruses including dengue, yellow fever, and West Nile viruses among humans and vectors in Guinea, informing policy decisions for public health objectives under the Simandou 2040 program.
brief.timeline_geography: 18 prefectures across four ecological zones (Lower, Middle, Upper, Forest) in Guinea, conducted between May 27 to November 27, 2024
brief.population_sample: N = unknown. Asymptomatic patients aged 1-90 years visited prefectural hospitals for consultations and gave consent. Patients who had not been vaccinated against yellow fever were included.
brief.key_methods: Venous blood sampling, mosquito collection via Aplecta Mosquito Trap light trap, ELISA tests for viral antibodies in human serum, real-time PCR to check for viral infection in vectors
key_findings: Seroprevalence of dengue virus antibodies: 18.22%
Seroprevalence of yellow fever virus antibodies: 23.86%
Seroprevalence of West Nile virus antibodies: 25.36%
brief.discussion: The study found that all three viruses are widely distributed across the country, with higher seroprevalence among certain prefectures, occupation groups, and ages. This implies a significant public health risk.
brief.limitations: Study limitations were not explicitly mentioned in the full text. However, cross-sectional studies are generally limited to describing associations and may not capture longitudinal changes or temporal relationships between variables.
brief.recommendations: The authors do not provide explicit policy recommendations from their findings.

brief.summary: Research demonstrates the susceptibility of various bird species to Usutu virus, a pathogen related to West Nile virus.
brief.objective: The authors sought to develop avian models of infection in the lab to better understand transmission and disease of Usutu virus in wild birds.
brief.timeline_geography: Multiple locations, including Europe over the past two decades
brief.population_sample: wild-caught house finches, wild-caught American robins, domestic canaries, and captive-bred zebra finches
brief.key_methods: Subcutaneous inoculation with Usutu virus isolates from Netherlands 2016 and Uganda 2012
key_findings: 100% of house finches became viremic when inoculated with USUV isolate Netherland 2016, whereas zebra finches did not become infected.
canaries are susceptible to USUV and develop moderate to severe clinical disease following virus dissemination.
American robins developed severe clinical signs of disease following USUV infection, including individual hepatocellular necrosis.
brief.discussion: These findings provide additional passerine bird models of infection that can be used to improve our understanding of Usutu virus transmission and disease. The use of these models will allow researchers to better understand the behavior of Usutu virus in wild birds and how it interacts with mosquitoes.
brief.limitations: The limitations of this study are acknowledged, including selection bias and under-reporting. However, the authors note that these biases did not appear to affect the results greatly.
brief.recommendations: The authors recommend further research into Usutu virus transmission dynamics in order to improve public health measures.

brief.summary: Timely and accurate diagnosis of dengue infection is critical for patient care and outbreak control. This study evaluates four serodiagnostics (ELISAs) to identify acute dengue infection from a single blood sample, proposing tailored approaches for improved diagnosis and epidemiological surveillance.
brief.objective: To evaluate the performance and combination of four enzyme-linked immunosorbent assays (ELISAs) for detecting dengue virus antigen (NS1) and antibodies (IgM and IgG) in various stages of infection, with implications for serodiagnostics and outbreak control.
brief.timeline_geography: 22 Vietnamese patients with RT-PCR-confirmed DENV infection, collected during acute (t1, 1–6 dpo), early convalescent (t2, 4–9 dpo), and late convalescent (t3, 13–19 dpo) phases.
brief.population_sample: 22 Vietnamese patients with RT-PCR-confirmed DENV infection
brief.key_methods: Sera from patients were tested using four ELISAss: NS1 ELISA, Anti-Dengue Virus Type 1–4 ELISA (IgM), Anti-Dengue Virus Type 1–4 ELISA (IgG; native antigen/gE-based), and the novel Anti-Dengue Virus NS1 ELISA 2.0 (IgG; recombinant NS1-based, with an alternative higher cut-off for flavivirus-endemic regions).
key_findings: Combing NS1 and IgM testing enables reliable identification of acute dengue infection from a single blood sample.
The novel Anti-Dengue Virus NS1 ELISA 2.0 shows improved detection performance in patients with Zika or West Nile virus exposure, reducing cross-reactivity.

brief.summary: This paper corrects errors in the author affiliations of a previous study on the association between avian biodiversity and West Nile Virus circulation in Culex mosquitoes in Emilia-Romagna, Italy.
brief.objective: To correct errors in the author affiliations of the original article

brief.summary: This study identifies the increasing threat of dengue virus circulation in Mali and other West African countries, highlighting the need to track arboviruses to inform public health policies.
brief.objective: To investigate the presence and distribution of arbovirus infections, including dengue, chikungunya, and West Nile viruses, among patients with acute undifferentiated fever in the Bamako region of Mali from 2016-2024.
brief.timeline_geography: The study was conducted in the Bamako region of Mali over a period of eight years (2016-2024).
brief.population_sample: A total of 210 patients with acute undifferentiated fever from 2016-2022, and 1,812 patients from 2023-2024 were included in the study. The majority of patients were female, ranging in age from 2 to 88 years.
brief.key_methods: The patients were tested using reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction (RT-qPCR) for the presence of various arboviruses.
key_findings: Dengue virus was detected in 16% of patients from 2016-2022, and 29% of patients from 2023-2024.
The proportion of positive samples was highest in 2019, with a majority of dengue cases (64.7%) reported during this year.
Co-infection with Plasmodium spp was found in 18.8% of dengue patients.
Hemorrhagic history was reported in two of the three patients with dengue infection.
The age distribution of DENV cases was similar to that of all tested cases from 2023-2024.
A total of 935 (51.6%) and 877 (48.4%) samples were positive for DENV among patients from 2024 and 2023 respectively.
brief.discussion: The increasing threat of dengue virus circulation in Mali highlights the need to strengthen public health policies to track arboviruses effectively.
brief.limitations: The main limitation of this study is that it covers a retrospective period with varying sample sizes.
brief.recommendations: Public health authorities in Mali and other West African countries should prioritize strategies for surveillance and control of dengue virus circulation, taking into account the geographical distribution of cases and vector breeding sites.

brief.summary: This paper presents a spatiotemporal analysis of Aedes aegypti and Culex quinquefasciatus populations in Miami-Dade County, Florida, identifying key hotspots and seasonal trends.
brief.objective: To identify resources at the local scale responsible for supporting mosquito populations, provide an early warning system for increased mosquito activity, and inform targeted control strategies to mitigate mosquito proliferation.
brief.timeline_geography: Miami-Dade County, Florida; eight-year study (2017-2024)
brief.population_sample: A total of 277 BG-Sentinel 2 traps and 31 CDC light traps were deployed over approximately 50 weeks per year.
brief.key_methods: BG-Sentinel and CDC traps baited with CO2, morphological identification of mosquitoes, analysis in R (version 4.2.2) using 'geosphere', 'rstudioapi', and 'dplyr' packages
key_findings: Ae. aegypti and Cx. quinquefasciatus remain present and collected in relatively high numbers throughout the year, suggesting continuous breeding and survival across seasons.
An average of 36 traps were classified as hotspots for Ae. aegypti, while an average of 35 traps was identified as hotspots for Cx. quinquefasciatus.
Culex quinquefasciatus remained more abundant overall compared to Ae. aegypti, with a mean abundance of 13.46 mosquitoes per trap-night.
brief.discussion: The seasonal population dynamics of Ae. aegypti and Cx. quinquefasciatus showed consistent temporal variations across the study period, underscoring their importance for year-round surveillance and situation awareness.
brief.limitations: Observational trends rather than results of inferential hypothesis testing were reported.
brief.recommendations: The authors recommend informed targeted control strategies to mitigate mosquito proliferation, which could include modified resource allocation based on hotspot classification.

brief.summary: Researchers conducted a study to evaluate the effectiveness of catch basin larvicide treatments in reducing adult mosquito populations, specifically Culex pipiens and Cx. restuans, in metropolitan Milwaukee, WI.
brief.objective: To assess whether larvicide treatments in catch basins can suppress Culex mosquito populations and reduce West Nile virus transmission risk.
brief.study_type: Experimental study using a stepped-wedge cluster trial (SWCT) design
brief.timeline_geography: Study took place in Milwaukee County, WI, USA from June to September 2019. Four 2.59 km^2 study sites were selected based on landscape composition similarity and comparable numbers of catch basins.
brief.population_sample: Adult Culex spp. mosquitoes (Culex pipiens and Cx. restuans) in residential areas
brief.key_methods: Larvicide treatments using VectoLex FG (a microbial control agent) were applied to catch basins at selected sites. Adult mosquito surveillance was conducted using CDC-baited light traps and gravid traps.
key_findings: Use of larvicide treatments reduced adult Culex spp. abundance in treated catch basins.
brief.discussion: The results suggest that larvicide treatments can be an effective tool for reducing West Nile virus transmission risk. However, further research is needed to understand the long-term efficacy and potential environmental impacts of such treatments.

brief.summary: This study analyzed hospitalization data in Canada from 2002 to 2023 to assess the impact of various mosquito-borne arboviruses. The authors found that some diseases are endemic (present in Canada and consistently reported), while others are non-endemic (have not been reported in humans acquired in Canada or detected via animal/vector surveillance).
brief.objective: To investigate hospitalizations associated with mosquito-transmitted arboviruses in Canada, identify endemic and non-endemic diseases, and assess the potential for non-endemic diseases to become endemic.
brief.timeline_geography: 2002-2023, Canada-wide, excluding Quebec
brief.population_sample: hospitalized patients with mosquito-transmitted arbovirus-related diagnoses
brief.key_methods: use of administrative hospital data and the Discharge Abstract Database (DAD), classification of diseases as endemic or non-endemic based on reported cases and pathogen detections
key_findings: West Nile virus, Eastern equine encephalitis, and other viruses are considered endemic to Canada.
California encephalitis, dengue, chikungunya, Zika, Japanese encephalitis, Rift valley fever, Australian encephalitis, and yellow fever are classified as non-endemic diseases in Canada.
brief.discussion: The authors discuss the potential implications of their findings for public health policy and future research.
brief.limitations: The study excludes hospitalization data from Quebec, which may affect the accuracy of results for certain regions. The classification of endemic versus non-endemic diseases is based on reported cases and pathogen detections, which may not be exhaustive or definitive.
brief.recommendations: None mentioned in the text.

brief.summary: A scoping review of 61 studies on the role of citizen science in mosquito-borne disease surveillance and control finds that it can enhance monitoring, but also highlights methodological gaps and inconsistencies in reporting.
brief.objective: This study aims to systematically examine citizen science applications in mosquito-borne diseases surveillance and control, with a focus on participation models, data types, platforms/tools, analytical approaches, epidemiologic outputs, and ethical considerations.
brief.timeline_geography: 2000-2025, global, primarily Europe (44.3%) and the Americas (21.3%)
brief.population_sample: mosquito-borne disease surveillance and control studies, involving public participation and citizen-generated data
brief.key_methods: comprehensive literature search across several databases, using controlled vocabulary and free-text keywords
key_findings: Citizen science can enhance mosquito surveillance, particularly for monitoring invasive species and spatio-temporal trends.
brief.discussion: The growing body of evidence indicates that citizen science has the potential to broaden the reach and improve the timeliness of MBDs surveillance. However, the methodological rigor and representativeness of these studies need improvement, as well as the inconsistency in reporting ethical and governance practices.
brief.limitations: The studies reviewed were mostly conducted in urban settings (47.5%), with relatively few in rural areas (18%); most were published after 2017 (93%)
brief.recommendations: Future research on citizen science-based MBDs surveillance should focus on addressing methodological gaps and inconsistencies, as well as prioritizing data-sharing and open-access policies to enhance operational use.

brief.summary: This study examines mosquito viromes associated with Vector-Borne diseases in Quebec, Canada, using RNA metagenomic profiling of over 44,000 mosquito pools collected between 2003 and 2016.
brief.objective: To investigate the viral diversity in mosquitoes linked to arboviruses in Quebec, Canada, and to identify potential vectors for these viruses.
brief.timeline_geography: Quebec, Canada; mosquito pools collected between 2003 and 2016, primarily from Greater Montreal area.
brief.population_sample: over 44,000 mosquito pools of various species, including Culex pipiens, Culiseta melanura, and Ochlerotatus stimulans.
brief.key_methods: RNA metagenomic profiling using CZ-ID platform, including quality-control steps such as host read removal, adapter trimming, and filtering for low-quality reads; consensus genome generation with sequencing depth >= 30x and overall assembly quality >= 96%.
key_findings: Multiple mosquito species were found to harbor arboviruses such as WNV, EEEV, and SSHV in Quebec, Canada.
RNA metagenomic profiling revealed a high degree of viral diversity among the mosquito pools.
Culex pipiens was identified as the primary vector for WNV.
brief.discussion: The study highlights the importance of considering multiple mosquito species when investigating the vector-borne transmission of arboviruses. The findings also underscore the need for continued surveillance and monitoring of these viruses in Quebec, Canada, to inform public health measures. Furthermore, the study suggests that the CZ-ID platform is a valuable tool for global pathogen detection and surveillance.
brief.limitations: The study was limited by the lack of thorough comparison of viromes across species due to insufficient availability of arbovirus-infected Culiseta or Ochlerotatus species. Additionally, the study only considered mosquito pools collected between 2003 and 2016, which may not be representative of current viral distributions in Quebec.
brief.recommendations: The authors recommend continued surveillance and monitoring of arboviruses in mosquitoes to inform public health measures, particularly in regions with high mosquito populations and potential for vector-borne transmission. Additionally, they suggest developing more standardized methods for RNA metagenomic profiling and virome analysis across different platforms.

brief.summary: This study investigated the viral replication dynamics of Zika virus (ZIKV), West Nile virus (WNV), and Mayaro virus (MAYV) in Vero cells through single infections, coinfections, and superinfections. The results showed significant interactions between the viruses, affecting their RNA production.
brief.objective: To understand the viral replication dynamics of ZIKV, WNV, and MAYV in Vero cells under different infection scenarios
brief.study_type: ex vivo study on virus-virus interactions
brief.timeline_geography: the experiments were performed in a laboratory at Brock University; no specific location or date is mentioned in the text
brief.population_sample: Vero cells from Cercopithecus aethiops, obtained from BEI Resources
brief.key_methods: Plaque assay and RT-qPCR for viral RNA quantification, Fiji software for image analysis
key_findings: Significant interactions between ZIKV, WNV, and MAYV in coinfections and superinfections.
RNA production was significantly increased (>1) for coinfected cells compared to single infections.
brief.discussion: The findings suggest that the presence of other viruses can impact viral replication, highlighting the complexity of viral interactions in the laboratory setting

brief.summary: This study investigates the finite-time stability of a stochastic West Nile virus model, providing new insights into disease transmission and control.
brief.objective: The authors aim to derive a sufficient condition for the finite-time stability of the West Nile virus model and analyze the influence of noise intensity, mortality rates, and transmission rates on this stability.
brief.study_type: Numerical simulations are conducted to verify theoretical results.
brief.timeline_geography: The study examines West Nile fever cases in several countries across Europe and the United States, particularly in Italy, Israel, and Greece.
brief.population_sample: Humans, birds, and mammals like horses and cattle are studied as reservoir hosts for the virus.
brief.key_methods: A stochastic West Nile virus model is constructed, with a Lyapunov function and the Gronwall inequality used to derive sufficient conditions for finite-time stability. Numerical simulations analyze how noise intensity, mortality rates, and transmission rates affect this stability.
key_findings: The lower the noise intensity and transmission rates, the greater the mortality rates, and the better the system can achieve finite-time stability.
brief.discussion: These findings suggest that reducing mosquito bites and controlling the spread of the virus through improved public health measures could be beneficial. The study highlights the importance of developing targeted interventions to mitigate the risk of West Nile virus infection.
brief.limitations: The authors acknowledge that their model assumes a simplified relationship between noise intensity, mortality rates, and transmission rates. Future work should aim to incorporate more realistic assumptions into the model.
brief.recommendations: Developing antiviral treatments or vaccines against West Nile virus would significantly reduce the risk of infection. In the meantime, focusing on public health measures such as vaccination of birds and controlling mosquito populations could help prevent outbreaks.

brief.summary: This study identifies a novel class of small molecules that target the NS2A protein, a previously underexplored viral protein in orthoflaviviruses, and demonstrates activity against multiple viruses.
brief.objective: To address the need for broadly effective antiviral drugs against orthoflaviviruses, this study aimed to discover new inhibitors targeting the NS2A protein using high-content screening.
brief.population_sample: orthoflavivirus viruses (DENV-2 as a representative)
brief.key_methods: High-content imaging (HCI) antiviral assay
key_findings: Novel multimodal orthoflavivirus inhibitor identified
Compound JNJ-1953 targets NS2A protein and reduces viral RNA synthesis, impairs packaging, and disrupts interactions with prM protein
brief.recommendations: Targeting NS2A protein could enable new therapeutic strategies to reduce the burden of orthoflavivirus infections worldwide.

brief.summary: An avian orthoflavivirus, Tembusu virus, loses its ability to produce infectious particles when the nonstructural protein 1 has N-glycosylation removed due to retention in the endoplasmic reticulum and enhanced interaction with E proteins.
brief.objective: Investigate how N-glycosylation of NS1 affects progeny virion assembly in orthoflaviviruses by comparing mutant viruses
brief.timeline_geography: Not mentioned explicitly, but presumably conducted in a laboratory setting with specific cell lines.
brief.population_sample: Various cell types (e.g., duck embryo fibroblast, Vero) infected with the wild-type and mutated Tembusu viruses.
brief.key_methods: Viral titration through TCID50 assays, RNA extraction via RNAiso Plus reagent, quantitative RT-qPCR using F488 SYBR qPCR Mix to determine TMUV genome copies.
key_findings: Removal of N-glycosylation from NS1 leads to reduced progeny virion assembly and production of infectious particles.
Retention of NS1 in the endoplasmic reticulum is enhanced by N-glycosylation loss
brief.discussion: These findings unveil a universal mechanism across several orthoflaviviruses, implying that efficient progeny viral particle production depends on NS1 glycosylation. The molecular pathway for NS1-N-glycosylation and its impact on progeny virion assembly is explored

brief.summary: Studies show a progressive expansion of West Nile virus (WNV) endemic progression in Europe due to rising temperatures, necessitating awareness and preparedness through integrated surveillance, blood donor screening, and diagnostic improvement.
brief.objective: This systematic review aims to investigate recent evidence on autochthonous human WNV infections in Europe, specifically examining geographic expansion, drivers, and implications for One Health strategies under climate change scenarios.
brief.timeline_geography: Europe, various countries including Austria, Greece, Romania, and Russia
brief.population_sample: humans (autochthonous infections) and animals (sentinel animals)
brief.key_methods: literature search of PubMed database from January 3rd, 2026; phylogenetic analysis of locally circulating WNV lineage 2 strains
key_findings: WNV has progressively expanded its geographic distribution in Europe over the past decade.
Rising temperatures were the most consistently reported meteorological correlate of WNV infection incidence and associated with earlier seasonal onset and prolonged transmission.
Between August 2020 and July 2021, a large autochthonous outbreak occurred in Lazio region (central Italy) affecting 171 individuals, including 57 cases of WNND
brief.discussion: The study findings suggest that awareness and preparedness for WNV endemic progression are vital. As climate change scenarios intensify, it is expected that WNV circulation will continue to expand geographically. The role of sentinel animals in detecting early signs of local circulation requires further investigation. An improved blood donor screening strategy and confirmatory diagnostic tools with enhanced serological discrimination in flaviviral co-circulation regions are indispensable.
brief.limitations: The study relies on published evidence from 2015 onwards, potentially introducing bias towards recent findings. Additionally, not all WNV infections or outbreaks may have been reported
brief.recommendations: Awareness and preparedness efforts must prioritize integrated surveillance, improved blood donor screening, and enhanced diagnostic capabilities in regions with flaviviral co-circulation.

brief.summary: The article reports that West Nile virus (WNV) caused the majority of arboviral disease cases in 2024, with 1,808 reported cases, of which 75% were neuroinvasive and resulted in a case-fatality rate of 13%. The virus was responsible for most deaths, with a total of 173 reported fatalities.
brief.objective: To investigate the epidemiology of nationally notifiable domestic arboviral diseases in the United States during 2024
brief.study_type: Retrospective cohort study analyzing surveillance reports from State health departments
brief.timeline_geography: Illness onset in 2024, reported from 48 states and the District of Columbia
brief.population_sample: Nationally notifiable domestic arboviral diseases with illness onset in 2024, including patients aged ≥60 years (1,133; 58%), male (1,223; 63%), and those with illness onset during July–September (1,603; 82%)
brief.key_methods: Surveillance reports from State health departments through ArboNET, the national arbovirus surveillance system
key_findings: West Nile virus caused the majority of reported arboviral disease cases (1,808; 92%) in 2024.
Powassan virus was the second most commonly reported arboviral disease (60; 3%), increasing from a previous high of 49 cases in 2023.
A total of 173 patients with WNV disease died, 169 (98%) of whom had neuroinvasive disease (case-fatality rate = 13% among patients with neuroinvasive disease)
brief.discussion: Variations in annual demographic characteristics, disease incidence, distribution, and seasonal temporality of arboviral diseases highlight the importance of quality and timely surveillance to increase awareness of disease risk, facilitate testing, and implement control measures.
brief.limitations: The study is limited by its reliance on voluntary reports from State health departments.
brief.recommendations: Clinicians should consider arboviral testing for patients with acute febrile or neurologic illness during periods when mosquitoes and ticks are active. Reducing arboviral disease morbidity and mortality relies on use of personal protective measures, implementing vector-control activities, and screening blood and organ donors for WNV.

brief.summary: A confirmed case of West Nile virus in a Brazilian municipality led to an epidemiological investigation, identifying 29 symptomatic residents and highlighting gaps in emerging arbovirus detection.
brief.objective: To describe the epidemiological investigation following laboratory confirmation of West Nile virus in an infant residing in Mato Grosso, Brazil.
brief.study_type: descriptive cross-sectional study with a territorial basis
brief.timeline_geography: February 11-13, 2026, Mato Grosso, Brazil (municipality Campo Novo do Parecis)
brief.population_sample: 112 residents within a 10-block radius of the index case's residence
brief.key_methods: Active surveillance: structured interviews and environmental data collection; Passive surveillance: retrospective search in municipal health system
key_findings: 1 confirmed case of West Nile virus in Mato Grosso, Brazil; 29 symptomatic individuals (25.9%) identified among 112 residents interviewed
brief.discussion: The investigation highlights the importance of rapid responses and situational assessments in emerging arbovirus cases.

brief.summary: This study estimates the risk of West Nile virus infection in seven European countries from 2008 to 2022 using serological and case notification data.
brief.objective: The authors aimed to model the spatial heterogeneity of West Nile virus transmission intensity across Europe and estimate the average percentage of human infections reported.
brief.timeline_geography: Seven European countries between 2008 and 2022, with serosurvey data from 21 countries.
brief.population_sample: Human population tested in published serosurveys with IgG-based assays in Europe (N = 92 datasets from 21 countries).
brief.key_methods: Mathematical models fitted to age-stratified serosurvey and case data, regression analysis for assay-specific seropositivity, catalytic model for regions with serosurvey data only.
key_findings: On average less than 0.2% of human West Nile virus infections were notified across Europe, with country variability.
brief.discussion: The study highlights the importance of spatial heterogeneity in transmission intensity and underscores the need to improve surveillance and reporting systems for West Nile virus.
brief.recommendations: The authors recommend improved surveillance, reporting systems, and vaccination strategies to mitigate the risk of West Nile virus infection.

brief.summary: A study of West Nile virus seroprevalence among blood donors in mainland France found low overall prevalence, with higher rates in Nouvelle-Aquitaine and Ile-de-France regions. Authors identify geographic living location (south of France) and ABO blood group as risk factors for WNV seropositivity.
brief.objective: To determine the seroprevalence of West Nile virus among blood donors in mainland France and investigate potential risk factors associated with seropositivity.
brief.timeline_geography: blood samples collected from 44,490 volunteer donors between November 2021 and June 2022 in metropolitan French departments, excluding the Creuse department
brief.population_sample: Healthy volunteers aged 18 to 70 years, with a total of 44,490 individual serum samples used for analysis
brief.key_methods: Enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA) using commercial IgG ELISA kits targeting the WNV envelope protein, followed by virus neutralisation test (VNT) confirmation against a panel of flaviviruses (DENV, TBEV, USUV, and WNV)
key_findings: The overall seroprevalence of West Nile virus was 0.87% in pooled samples and 0.97% in individual samples.
Prevalence rates were higher in Nouvelle-Aquitaine (1.13%) and Ile-de-France regions (1.81%), preceding the first local human cases reported in 2023 and 2025, respectively.
brief.discussion: The study's results suggest a low level of West Nile virus circulation among blood donors in mainland France. The findings are consistent with previous research indicating that WNV is mainly present in specific geographic areas, such as the south of France.
brief.limitations: None mentioned explicitly in the paper
brief.recommendations: None provided

brief.summary: This Scientific Report identifies potential entry pathways for 25 vector-borne diseases into currently free EU Member States, focusing on pathway identification rather than risk estimation.
brief.objective: To address Term of Reference (ToR) 1.4 by identifying and structuring the potential entry pathways for selected vector-borne diseases into previously free EU Member States
brief.study_type: Preparatory report supporting subsequent EU-level risk assessments
key_findings: Movement of ticks attached to livestock, wildlife, or pets is the only relevant vector-related entry pathway for tick-borne pathogens.
Wind-borne dispersal of adult midges is considered a potential entry pathway for Culicoides-borne pathogens, while active flight and passive transport are relevant only over short distances.
Introduction of adult mosquitoes via aircraft is considered a potential entry pathway for mosquito-borne pathogens.
brief.discussion: The report highlights the complexity of vector-borne diseases and the need for a structured framework to support EU-level risk assessments. The authors emphasize the importance of considering both vector-related and non-vectorial pathways in disease introduction.
brief.limitations: The conservative, inclusion-based approach applied may exclude some relevant pathways, and further quantitative risk assessment will address uncertainty.

brief.summary: The European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control (ECDC) and the European Food Safety Authority (EFSA) report three locally acquired human West Nile virus infections in two European countries, Italy and North Macedonia, with a total of five WNV outbreaks reported in birds and equids across the continent.
brief.objective: To summarise the current situation of West Nile virus infections in humans and animals in Europe as of June 2026, based on monthly reports submitted to ECDC and EFSA.
brief.timeline_geography: Europe, up to 24 June 2026
brief.population_sample: Three locally acquired human cases (Italy = 2, North Macedonia = 1) and five WNV outbreaks in birds and equids across the continent
brief.key_methods: None specified
key_findings: 3 human West Nile virus infections reported in Europe (Italy: 2, North Macedonia: 1)
5 West Nile virus outbreaks reported in birds and equids across the continent
brief.discussion: The authors note that the reported case numbers likely underestimate the true number of infections due to delays in diagnosis and reporting. They also anticipate further human cases and outbreaks in equids and birds to be reported in the coming weeks and months, given favourable weather conditions for WNV transmission.
brief.limitations: The current situation is based on monthly reports, which may not capture the complete picture of WNV infections and outbreaks in Europe.
brief.recommendations: None specified

brief.summary: Dengue virus detected in mosquitoes in Dubai, highlighting the need for integrated entomologic and molecular surveillance and public awareness campaigns.
brief.objective: To investigate the distribution of Aedes aegypti mosquitoes and detect the presence of Dengue Virus (DENV) in them, coinciding with a human DENV-2 outbreak in Dubai.
brief.study_type: Detection of pathogens in mosquito population, coinciding with a human disease outbreak
brief.timeline_geography: Dubai, United Arab Emirates, during a DENV-2 outbreak in 2026
brief.population_sample: Aedes aegypti mosquitoes from 2 sampling locations within the urban area of Dubai)
brief.key_methods: Entomologic surveillance and molecular detection (detection of DENV-1 and DENV-2 using PCR).
key_findings: Detection of DENV-1 and DENV-2 in Ae. aegypti mosquitoes from 2 sampling locations within the urban area of Dubai, coinciding with a DENV-2 outbreak in humans.
Presence of Ae. aegypti mosquitoes in urban areas in the Gulf region
brief.discussion: The findings demonstrate the value of integrated entomologic and molecular surveillance for early detection of mosquitoborne pathogens in arid urban settings.
brief.recommendations: Public awareness campaigns to educate people on avoiding mosquito bites, along with targeted mosquito control measures and isolating infected individuals quickly to prevent spread.

brief.summary: Miconazole, an antifungal medication, demonstrates broad-spectrum antiviral activity against West Nile virus (WNV) by downregulating the host protein thioredoxin-like 1 (TXNL1), leading to reduced viral replication and improved survival rates in mice.
brief.objective: To identify potential anti-WNV candidates from a blood-brain barrier-penetrating FDA-approved compound library and evaluate their antiviral efficacy against multiple flaviviruses, including WNV and other neurotropic flaviviruses like JE (Japanese encephalitis) virus and TBE (tick-borne encephalitis) virus.
brief.study_type: (retrospective cohort of existing compound library and surveillance analysis in mouse model.
brief.population_sample: Mice challenged with low dose West Nile virus via intracranial injection
brief.key_methods: High-throughput screening (HTS) using an FDA-approved compound library, cell viability assays, and mechanistic studies of miconazole action.
key_findings: Inhibition of WNV replication by miconazole in vitro up to 100%, with no significant toxicity observed at any dose tested. Selectivity indexes were 158.13 and 50.05 for Huh7 cells and SH-SY5Y (human neuroblastoma cell line) cells, respectively.

Viral load reduction in brain tissue and improvement of survival rates in mice treated with miconazole compared to controls, indicating antiviral efficacy against WNV infection in a murine model of CNS.
Miconazole exerts broad-spectrum activity against other flavivirus family members YFV (Yellow Fever virus), JEV (Japanese Encephalitis virus), and TBEV (Tick-Borne Encephalitis virus).
key_methods, discussion, limitations, recommendations)
brief.discussion: The broad-spectrum antiviral activity of miconazole suggests that it may target a common host factor essential for the flavivirus life cycle.
brief.limitations: None stated in provided text.
brief.recommendations: Potential use as antiviral therapy for West Nile virus (WNV) and other neurotropic flaviviruses, especially useful where rapid-acting interventions are needed to prevent or minimize CNS infection-related symptoms.

brief.summary: An outbreak investigation reported Usutu virus (USUV) emergence in the Campania region of Southern Italy. The authors detected USUV infection in a yellow-legged gull and Culex pipiens mosquito pool, with genetic sequences indicating a close relationship with European strains. The study highlights ongoing USUV circulation in Italy and Europe.
brief.objective: To investigate the presence and dynamics of Usutu virus (USUV) in the Campania region of Southern Italy
brief.timeline_geography: Campania region, Southern Italy; present study (year not specified)
brief.population_sample: yellow-legged gull, Eurasian jay, Culex pipiens mosquito pool (n=3 samples)
brief.key_methods: real-time RT-PCR analysis to detect USUV
key_findings: USUV detected in a yellow-legged gull and Culex pipiens mosquito pool
genetic sequences indicate close relationship with European strains (EU2-A lineage)
limited divergence observed across analyzed NS5 fragment
brief.discussion: The study provides evidence of ongoing USUV circulation in Italy, consistent with previous detections in the Veneto, Umbria, and other regions. The genetic sequencing results suggest a high level of conservation among USUV strains circulating globally

brief.summary: This review proposes a unifying hypothesis that virus-associated memory impairment represents a convergent hippocampal syndrome driven by shared downstream pathways, and suggests combination therapies targeting these pathways offer greater therapeutic promise than pathogen-specific approaches alone.
brief.objective: The authors aim to understand the convergence of various pathologies leading to memory impairment and propose a shared molecular architecture underlying different neurological conditions.
brief.timeline_geography: Not specified in the text, but it refers to various pathogens that affect the central nervous system worldwide.
brief.population_sample: Not explicitly stated in the text; however, based on the context, it is likely referring to a population affected by viral infections and neurodegenerative diseases.
brief.key_methods: Mechanistic stratification using emerging plasma biomarkers (p-tau217, neurofilament light chain, GFAP) combined with hippocampal subfield MRI.
key_findings: The four shared molecular pathways that selectively damage hippocampal circuits are: mitochondria-associated membrane dysfunction, chronic neuroinflammation, blood–brain barrier disruption, and impaired CREB-BDNF signaling.
brief.discussion: Understanding the convergent nature of these pathologies can help in developing combination therapeutic research targeting these common pathways.
brief.limitations: The review acknowledges that the strength of evidence varies across different pathogens and conditions. Direct mechanistic evidence, mechanistic analogy, and preclinical data are distinguished throughout the text.
brief.recommendations: The authors propose using combination therapies to target the shared molecular pathways simultaneously as a more promising approach than pathogen-specific treatments alone.

brief.summary: Hydroxytyrosol may be a promising candidate for further investigation as a virucidal agent against enveloped viruses.
brief.objective: To investigate the synthetic hydroxytyrosol (HT) antiviral properties against enveloped and non-enveloped viruses using in silico and in vitro methods.
brief.key_methods: Molecular docking and ADMET analyses, in vitro tests
key_findings: Substantial viral load decreases at 1000 µg/mL against several enveloped viruses
Viral titer of the measles virus decreased by 4.62 log10 units during the 2 h of exposure
brief.discussion: The specificity of hydroxytyrosol for enveloped viruses may be due to its ability to interact with lipid rafts and membrane microdomains enriched with sterols and sphingolipids, which are crucial for viral entry and fusion processes.

brief.summary: The study evaluated the performance of the STANDARD M10 Arbovirus Panel in diagnosing dengue and detecting other arboviruses. The results show that the panel has a high clinical accuracy for dengue, but its analytical sensitivity is inadequate for DENV-2 and CHIKV.
brief.objective: The study aimed to assess the clinical diagnostic accuracy of the STANDARD M10 Arbovirus Panel in diagnosing dengue and evaluate its analytical sensitivity across all eight panel targets. The objective also included characterizing detection thresholds for targets not represented by clinical specimens.
brief.timeline_geography: the Americas, 2024-2025
brief.population_sample: 163 de-identified serum samples classified using a composite reference standard consisting of Panbio NS1 ELISA reactivity (≥11 Panbio units) combined with compatible clinical and epidemiological data.
brief.key_methods: serial dilution experiments, RT-qPCR assays as the comparator.
key_findings: the M10 demonstrated sensitivity of 96.0% for dengue
operational LoDs were equivalent or superior to reference RT-qPCR for six targets (DENV-1, DENV-3, DENV-4, ZIKV, WNV, YFV)
reduced sensitivity for DENV-2 and CHIKV
brief.discussion: The study demonstrates that the STANDARD M10 Arbovirus Panel has high clinical accuracy for dengue but its analytical sensitivity is inadequate for DENV-2 and CHIKV. These results support the use of the panel as a complementary decentralized molecular tool, but highlight the need for future validation studies to address key limitations.
brief.limitations: reduced sensitivity for DENV-2 and CHIKV
brief.recommendations: future validation studies should focus on improving analytical sensitivity for DENV-2 and CHIKV.

brief.summary: This study examines whether online information-seeking patterns reflected official WNV surveillance during 2024-2025 in Greece, with a focus on the Crete region's One Health preparedness context.
brief.objective: To investigate if Google Trends and Wikipedia pageviews can accurately reflect national surveillance data for West Nile virus (WNV) cases in Greece, with a particular emphasis on regional One Health preparedness in Crete.
brief.timeline_geography: Greece, Crete region
brief.key_methods: Comparative analysis between national surveillance data and Google Trends/ Wikipedia pageviews for West Nile neuroinvasive disease/central nervous system (WNND/CNS) cases.
key_findings: Wikipedia pageviews showed a strong association with WNND/CNS activity in 2024 (Spearman rho = 0.802; p < 0.001) and 2025 (rho = 0.763; p < 0.001).
Google Trends associations were weaker at the same lag (2024: rho = 0.402, p = 0.003; 2025: rho = 0.452, p < 0.001).
brief.discussion: The digital indicators reflected concurrent or lagging public attention and did not demonstrate predictive capacity.

brief.summary: [WNV infection remodels host miRNA–mRNA regulatory landscape by altering interferon-related responses, NF-κB and MAPK signalling pathways, RNA processing, splicing, and proteasomal degradation. Candidate regulatory hubs involved in WNV-induced transcriptome remodelling are identified.]
brief.objective: Investigate how West Nile virus (WNV) infection remodels the host miRNA–mRNA regulatory landscape.
brief.timeline_geography: HEK-293 cells
brief.population_sample: N/A
brief.key_methods: miRNA-seq, RNA-seq, Gene Ontology and pathway enrichment analyses, integrated miRNA–mRNA network reconstruction using Cytoscape.
key_findings: WNV infection induced global changes in host miRNA expression. Candidate regulatory hubs involved in WNV-induced transcriptome remodelling are identified.
Different WNV strains produce overlapping or strain-specific miRNA landscape alterations.
Different pathways associated with RNA processing, splicing, and proteasomal degradation are downregulated.
brief.discussion: [The study highlights the role of host miRNAs in modulating antiviral responses and virus–host dynamics. These findings provide a foundation for future experimental validation.]

brief.summary: A study published in Genes found that Mosla chinensis essential oil has a significant repellent effect against Culex quinquefasciatus mosquitoes, potentially reducing the risk of vector-borne diseases.
brief.objective: To explore the olfactory repellent molecular mechanism of plant essential oils and investigate their potential as mosquito control agents
brief.timeline_geography: Wuhan, China
brief.population_sample: Culex quinquefasciatus mosquitoes
brief.key_methods: GC-MS analysis, olfactory behavior experiments, fluorescence competitive binding assays, molecular docking and site-directed mutation analysis
key_findings: Mosla chinensis essential oil showed a significant repellent effect against C. quinquefasciatus
The odorant-binding protein 1 and odorant-binding protein 2 genes (CquiOBP1-2) exhibited great binding capacities to volatile components in the essential oil
Molecular docking and site-directed mutation analysis confirmed key amino acid residues involved in the olfactory recognition of repellent ligand compounds
brief.discussion: The study helps promote the biological control of plant essential oils in mosquito pests, providing new insights into their molecular mechanism of action

brief.summary: Molecular diagnosis of West Nile virus (WNV) infections can benefit from a new workflow that combines PMAxx treatment with digital PCR to improve molecular discrimination between infectious and non-infectious viral particles.
brief.objective: This study evaluates the effectiveness of using a digital PCR-based workflow with PMAxx treatment, which selectively targets non-intact WNV particles, thereby enhancing the detection of truly infectious viruses in patients.
brief.timeline_geography: 41 patients from Italy, predominantly diagnosed with West Nile fever (WNF) or neuroinvasive disease (WNND)
brief.population_sample: 55 patient samples and biological fluids including plasma and urine, tested without and with PMAxx pretreatment for WNV RNA detection.
brief.key_methods: Digital PCR combined with PMAxx treatment to evaluate viral integrity.
key_findings: 50% reduction in detectable virus in the presence of PMA
viral load in urine was higher than in plasma, but decreased significantly after application of PMA
dPCR increased detection rates by 20% in comparison with RT-PCR.

brief.summary: This review article discusses herpesvirus-vectored vaccines as a promising platform for veterinary applications. It provides an analysis of five well-characterized alphaherpesviruses and their performance compared to traditional vaccine platforms.
brief.objective: The study aims to provide a comprehensive understanding of the state of the art in herpesvirus-vectored vaccines for veterinary applications, highlighting key advances in vectored vaccine development.
key_findings: Herpesvirus-vectored vaccines represent a versatile platform for enhancing animal health, supporting sustainable agriculture, and mitigating zoonotic risks.
These approaches demonstrate protective efficacy against a range of significant animal pathogens.
brief.discussion: The authors highlight the advantages of herpesvirus-vectored vaccines over traditional vaccine platforms. They also discuss future directions in vector engineering, mucosal delivery, and synthetic biology approaches.

brief.summary: Opportunistic infections in pediatric kidney transplant recipients are a significant concern, with half of infectious episodes occurring beyond the first post-transplant year. The authors analyzed 10 years of data from their center and found that BK virus was the most frequent pathogen, followed by fungal infections and cytomegalovirus.
brief.objective: To investigate the timing and clinical impact of opportunistic infections in pediatric kidney transplant recipients
brief.timeline_geography: a single tertiary center between 2014 and 2024 (Thessaloniki, Greece)
brief.population_sample: 27 pediatric kidney transplant recipients with a mean follow-up of 5.6 years
brief.key_methods: retrospective review of demographic and clinical characteristics, infection type, timing after transplantation, management, and outcomes
key_findings: 20.7% of patients developed at least one clinically significant opportunistic infection; BK virus was the most frequent pathogen (45.5%), followed by fungal infections and cytomegalovirus; five episodes (45.5%) occurred within the first post-transplant year, while six (54.5%) occurred later during follow-up
brief.limitations: limited pre-transplant exposure to common viral pathogens may increase the risk of primary infection after transplantation
brief.recommendations: Preventive strategies, including pre-transplant immunization and post-transplant surveillance protocols, remain essential components of transplant care

brief.summary: This article discusses the role of the blood-cerebrospinal fluid barrier (BCSFB) in arboviral encephalitis, challenging existing blood-brain barrier-centered frameworks and highlighting the importance of considering the contribution of other CNS border structures.
brief.objective: The authors aim to re-examine the BCSFB as a relevant neuroinvasion interface in arboviral encephalitis, emphasizing its potential contribution beyond the BBB-centric view.
key_findings: Zika virus infection can infect pericytes in the choroid plexus and reach the CNS through the blood-CSF interface
brief.discussion: While evidence for BCSFB involvement is strongest for Zika virus, its contribution remains indirect or insufficiently resolved for other clinically important arboviruses.
brief.limitations: Current evidentiary landscape remains uneven, with asymmetry in direct support across arboviruses; authors acknowledge this fact explicitly, arguing not to replace BBB-centered models.
brief.recommendations: Research is needed to directly test the role of BCSFB in encephalitic disease for each virus; a hierarchical, virus-dependent view of choroid plexus involvement is suggested.

brief.summary: Syphilitic panuveitis is a severe manifestation of ocular syphilis that can mimic non-infectious or viral uveitis and delay etiologic recognition. Rhegmatogenous retinal detachment is a vision-threatening complication that requires timely antimicrobial therapy and early involvement of vitreoretinal surgery.
brief.objective: To provide a comprehensive review of the clinical presentation, imaging findings, pathophysiology, and management of syphilitic panuveitis and associated rhegmatogenous retinal detachment
brief.timeline_geography: Studies analyzed from January 2000 to September 10, 2025, with a focus on relevant endemic or seasonal settings.
brief.population_sample: Patients with ocular manifestations of syphilis and associated rhegmatogenous retinal detachment. HIV coinfection was also examined as modifying disease severity
brief.key_methods: Medline, Scopus, Web of Science databases were searched for publications in English from January 2000 to September 10, 2025. PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science keywords combinations included syphilis, ocular syphilis and infection-oriented diagnostic methods were also considered.
key_findings: Posterior uveitis and panuveitis are common clinical presentations of ocular syphilis which can be bilateral and frequently accompanied by dense vitritis, retinal vasculitis and optic nerve problems

Rhegmatogenous retinal detachment is a vision-threatening complication that likely reflects advanced inflammation-induced damage at the vitreoretinal interface. It may arise due to retinal necrosis, persistent vitreoretinal traction, and early proliferative vitreoretinopathy.
HIV coinfection can modify disease severity in patients with ocular syphilis and associated rhegmatogenous retinal detachment.
brief.recommendations: Routine testing for syphilis and HIV is essential to reduce diagnostic delay. Early recognition of syphilitic panuveitis, particularly posterior uveitis or panuveitis, requires antimicrobial therapy and may require immediate involvement of vitreoretinal surgery.

brief.summary: Hospitalized patients with WNV infection may present with heterogeneous clinical phenotypes extending beyond classical neuroinvasive disease. Neurological involvement appears to be the main clinical marker of adverse outcome, while selected hematological parameters may provide preliminary prognostic information.
brief.objective: To describe the real-world clinical spectrum of WNV infection in hospitalized patients admitted to internal medicine wards during a localized outbreak in Southern Italy and to explore clinical and hematological variables associated with short-term mortality and in-hospital outcomes.
brief.timeline_geography: A localized seasonal outbreak in Southern Italy.
brief.population_sample: Consecutive adult patients admitted to internal medicine wards of four hospitals.
brief.key_methods: Laboratory-confirmed WNV infection diagnosis, hematological parameters, and clinical characteristics analysis.
key_findings: In-hospital mortality was 43% and early mortality within 10 days occurred in 17%. Neurological involvement was significantly more frequent among non-survivors and associated with increased in-hospital mortality. Higher monocyte percentages were associated with overall mortality, whereas eosinopenia, leukopenia, and thrombocytopenia were associated with early mortality.
brief.discussion: The authors interpret these findings against existing data on WNV infection. They note that the clinical spectrum of WNV infection is remarkably heterogeneous and extends beyond classical neuroinvasive disease. Neurological involvement appears to be the main clinical marker of adverse outcome, while selected hematological parameters may provide preliminary prognostic information.
brief.limitations: The limited sample size and retrospective design limit the findings. The authors consider these results hypothesis-generating rather than definitive.
brief.recommendations: None provided.

brief.summary: This case report describes a rare instance of multifocal dysembryoplastic neuroepithelial tumors (DNETs), where a 47-year-old woman developed intracranial and spinal DNETs treated surgically. Despite being the oldest reported case, she achieved seizure freedom post-resection.
brief.objective: The authors aim to present a case of disseminated intracranial and spinal dysembryoplastic neuroepithelial tumors (DNETs), systematically review existing literature on DNETs, and underscore the potential need for spinal MRI in intracranial DNET cases and multidisciplinary management.
brief.timeline_geography: 2026; Poland
brief.population_sample: 1 patient (47-year-old woman)
brief.key_methods: MRI, surgical intervention (craniotomy/laminectomy), EEG
key_findings: intracranial DNETs occur in both locations primary tumors and secondary lesions predominantly spinal, obstructive hydrocephalus occurs in 67% often requiring shunting epilepsy is rare n = 1, 17%
fatal outcomes possibly associated with West Nile virus infection (S100B protein pathway)
brief.discussion: The authors highlight the rarity of spinal involvement attributed to embryologic origins and potential need for spinal MRI in intracranial DNET cases. They also emphasize the challenges of multifocal presentation and importance of multidisciplinary management.
brief.limitations: Small sample size limited literature review no external funding
brief.recommendations: Further molecular studies case registries are crucial to understand pathogenesis and optimize care.

brief.summary: Horses can serve as effective sentinel hosts for detecting viral circulation and predicting public health risks due to their frequent exposure to mosquito vectors and ability to mount measurable antibody responses.
brief.objective: To examine the role of horses as sentinel hosts in West Nile virus surveillance within a One Health framework and to provide evidence-based insights into the epidemiological significance of equine WNV infections.
key_findings: Equine seroprevalence and field surveillance can identify transmission hotspots, reveal silent circulation, and contribute to the understanding of spatial and temporal risk patterns.
brief.discussion: The value of horses as sentinel hosts is particularly relevant within a One Health framework where interactions between wildlife reservoirs, arthropod vectors, domestic animals, humans, and environmental conditions collectively shape the transmission dynamics of West Nile virus. In this review, we examined WNV in hores as an intermediate and strategically informative position.

brief.summary: This article compiles and analyzes over 100 plant alkaloids against neglected arboviruses, revealing potent activity against flaviviruses and highlighting key pharmacophoric features.
brief.objective: The authors investigate the potential of plant alkaloids as broad-spectrum antiviral scaffolds against neglected arboviruses, with a focus on flavivirus families.
brief.timeline_geography: Multiple articles studied over 5 years from diverse plant families published between June and August 2026
key_findings: Narciclasine exhibits potent activity against DENV, ZIKV, YFV, and JEV with an EC50 of 0.02 µM
brief.discussion: The study reveals that several plant alkaloids, including lycorine, narciclasine, emetine, and berbamine, show strong antiviral activity against flaviviruses, which could lead to the development of novel broad-spectrum treatments for these viruses. Additionally, genetic resistance data suggests that ribosome-mediated translational stress may represent an additional host-directed antiviral mechanism.
brief.limitations: This analysis was based on in vitro data and the mechanisms proposed require direct validation. Moreover, the involvement of multiple alkaloids and potential cross-reactivity between them may complicate their therapeutic use.
brief.recommendations: Due to this lack of validation, unbiased target deconvolution and formal testing of the ribosome/integrated stress response hypothesis are essential research priorities

brief.summary: A mosquito abatement district in Idaho modernized its surveillance and detection methods to improve the capacity to detect arboviral diseases, leading to a confirmed sighting of Aedes aegypti.
brief.objective: The authors aimed to develop a more effective arbovirus surveillance system that could standardize mosquito identification and pooling procedures, implement triplex RT-qPCR testing, and increase laboratory capacity to reduce reliance on external confirmatory testing.
brief.timeline_geography: southernwestern Idaho, 2021-2025
brief.population_sample: mosquitoes (Culex spp., Aedes aegypti)
brief.key_methods: Triplex RT-qPCR testing, DNA barcoding, morphological identification, mosquito pooling procedures
key_findings: The Canyon County Mosquito Abatement District's integrated approach improved arboviral surveillance, confirming recurrent WNV activity and  the presence of Aedes aegypti in Idaho for the first time.
Enhanced laboratory capacity reduced sample-processing times and costs, enabling same-day reporting and reducing reliance on external services.
brief.discussion: The study's findings highlight the importance of modernizing arbovirus surveillance systems to improve detection accuracy, response capabilities, and public health outcomes. The authors emphasize that local mosquito abatement districts need stronger diagnostic capacity and integrated data systems for rapid detection and response.
brief.limitations: None explicitly stated in the text
brief.recommendations: The study recommends prioritizing enhanced laboratory capacity and molecular diagnostic techniques for improved surveillance and response to arboviral diseases, as well as integrating site metadata and spatial analysis to support multi-year comparisons.

brief.summary: This study examines how temperature affects West Nile Virus (WNV) activity in Croatia, with implications for public health.
brief.objective: To investigate the relationship between weather conditions and WNV transmission dynamics in endemic regions of continental Croatia.
brief.timeline_geography: Croatia, 2015-2024, two endemic regions: East Croatia and Central Croatia
brief.population_sample: Horses (equine seroprevalence) and humans with WNV cases in Croatia
brief.key_methods: Analysis of climatological data (temperature, rainfall, humidity), equine seroprevalence, human case data
key_findings: Mean April temperatures were a significant predictor of human WNV cases.
Higher temperatures in February, April, May, and October were associated with increased WNV activity.

brief.summary: A study published in Pathogens suggests that Tick-Borne Encephalitis (TBE) may be underrecognized in Serbia, as confirmatory testing revealed TBE-neutralizing antibodies in four of 79 patients with suspected West Nile Virus (WNV) infection.
brief.objective: To investigate the presence of TBEV-neutralizing antibodies in serum samples from patients hospitalized between 2018 and 2023 with suspected WNV neuroinvasive disease or viral encephalitis of unknown etiology in Serbia, to better define the burden of TBE and inform prevention strategies.
brief.timeline_geography: Between 2018 and 2023 in Serbia
brief.population_sample: 79 patients hospitalized with suspected WNV neuroinvasive disease or viral encephalitis of unknown etiology
brief.key_methods: Microneutralization assay for detecting TBEV-neutralizing antibodies
key_findings: 4 out of 79 patients (5.1%) had detectable TBEV-neutralizing antibodies
Most reactive cases occurred in patients initially classified as having suspected WNV-associated meningoencephalitis
brief.discussion: The findings suggest that TBE may be underrecognized in Serbia, highlighting the importance of confirmatory testing in orthoflavivirus-endemic settings. Strengthening clinical awareness and surveillance will be essential to better define the burden of TBE and inform prevention strategies.
brief.limitations: Limited sample size (79 patients) and retrospective study design
brief.recommendations: Strengthening clinical awareness and surveillance to better define the burden of TBE and inform prevention strategies.

brief.summary: Replacing disposable styrofoam cups with alternative materials in larval mosquito bioassays can significantly affect the estimated susceptibility of mosquitoes to S-methoprene.
brief.objective: To evaluate the effect of different cup materials on measured S-methoprene concentration-response relationships and identify a suitable replacement for standardized larval bioassays.
brief.study_type: Comparative study of alternative cup materials in larval mosquito bioassays
brief.timeline_geography: Laboratory experiments conducted using a reference colony of Culex quinquefasciatus mosquitoes reared under laboratory-controlled conditions.
brief.population_sample: Culex quinquefasciatus (CQ1) mosquitoes, originally collected in Merced County, CA, in the 1950s
brief.key_methods: Bioassays using S-methoprene concentrations and probit regression to estimate LC50 and LC90 estimates for each cup type.
key_findings: HDPE and paper cups produced significantly higher LC50 and LC90 estimates than Styrofoam, while PET and PP responses were comparable to Styrofoam.
Concentration-response slopes were similar among cup materials.
brief.recommendations: Replacement assay cups should be validated before implementation in larval resistance monitoring programs.

brief.summary: This study reports the first Usutu virus (USUV) infection in an asymptomatic blood donor in Greece, with implications for public health surveillance.
brief.objective: To describe the first cases of USUV infection in Greece and to investigate the genetic lineage of the strain.
brief.timeline_geography: late September 2024, Central Macedonia in northern Greece
brief.population_sample: one asymptomatic blood donor, a female in her late 20s
brief.key_methods: whole genome sequencing, phylogenetic analysis using Ion Torrent next-generation sequencing platform
key_findings: The strain clusters within the USUV Europe 2A genetic lineage.
USUV RNA was detected in cell culture, confirming the infection.
brief.discussion: The detection of USUV human infection in Greece prompts for further studies to elucidate its epidemiology and ecology in the country.

brief.summary: This article examines how climate change is reshaping the epidemiology of vector-borne diseases in Europe, using dengue as a sentinel example. The authors argue that strengthened surveillance and preparedness systems are essential to prevent repeated introductions from becoming sustained public-health challenges.
brief.objective: The study objective is to analyze the impact of climate change on autochthonous vector-borne disease transmission in Europe and to examine the role of dengue as a sentinel example of a wider climate-sensitive transition.
brief.timeline_geography: Europe, Southern and Central Europe
brief.population_sample: None stated specifically
brief.key_methods: Use of surveillance data, laboratory capacity, frontline clinical awareness, cross-sectoral response systems to predict and prevent local outbreaks
key_findings: Rising temperatures are increasing the suitability of parts of Europe for competent mosquito vectors.
Human mobility and land-use change increase the probability that imported pathogens encounter permissive conditions for local transmission.

Dengue is used as a sentinel example because it demonstrates how imported viraemic cases, established competent Aedes vectors and delayed clinical recognition can converge to produce local transmission.
brief.discussion: The authors argue that strengthening climate-informed surveillance, rapid laboratory capacity, frontline clinical awareness, and cross-sectoral response systems will be essential to prevent repeated introductions from becoming sustained public-health challenges.
brief.limitations: None stated specifically
brief.recommendations: Strengthening climate-informed surveillance, rapid laboratory capacity, frontline clinical awareness, and cross-sectoral response systems.

brief.summary: Viruses exploit cellular mechanisms such as endoplasmic reticulum (ER) stress, unfolded protein response (UPR), and lipid droplet (LD) dynamics to enhance their replication.
brief.objective: To understand how flaviviruses, a group of RNA viruses including dengue virus, Zika virus, and others, manipulate host cellular mechanisms such as ER stress, UPR, and LD dynamics to optimize their life cycles.
brief.population_sample: Human cells infected with flaviviruses
brief.key_methods: Analysis of molecular mechanisms underlying flavivirus infection
key_findings: Flaviviruses activate the UPR branches PERK, IRE1, and ATF6 to optimize viral translation, replication, and egress
Infection leads to dynamic changes in lipid droplets (LDs), key organelles for lipid storage and viral replication

brief.summary: The development of a vaccine for West Nile Virus (WNV) is hindered by scientific, regulatory, and economic challenges, including complex immunopathogenesis and cross-reactive immune responses among flaviviruses.
brief.objective: To review the latest progress and challenges in developing vaccines against WNV, highlighting the need for accelerated research to overcome existing barriers.
key_findings: No licensed vaccine is available for human use despite several candidates demonstrating promising results in preclinical studies and early clinical trials.
brief.discussion: The development of a safe and effective WNV vaccine must balance minimizing safety issues with achieving high protective immunity.
brief.limitations: Progress has been slow due to the complex immunopathogenesis of WNV, cross-reactive immune responses among flaviviruses, and economic barriers.

brief.summary: West Nile Virus as a Trigger for Cardiovascular Diseases: A Meta-summary of Case Reports.
brief.objective: To understand the cardiovascular complications following West Nile virus infection by reviewing case reports and analyzing their clinical features
brief.timeline_geography: Cases were identified between 2009-2023 across multiple datasets, with authors unable to provide consistent hospital stay data or timing of cardiac complications.
brief.population_sample: 8 patients who developed cardiovascular complications following a WNV infection, median age 67.29 years (53-70) and 87.5% male.
key_findings: 62.5% of patients had impaired left ventricular ejection fraction

brief.summary: This study from the Johns Hopkins Health System identifies adults with confirmed or probable West Nile virus (WNV) infections between 2013 and 2024. A total of 86 cases were analyzed, and the results highlight several risk factors for WNV neuroinvasive disease (WNND).
brief.objective: To identify risk factors for West Nile virus (WNV) neuroinvasive disease (WNND) in adults within the Johns Hopkins Health System.
brief.timeline_geography: January 1, 2013, to December 31, 2024, in Maryland, Washington D.C., and Florida (but only pediatric facilities were excluded from this analysis)
brief.population_sample: 367 adult patients with positive ICD-10 codes or laboratory results for WNV
brief.key_methods: Cohort selection using the Epic Clarity database with search criteria for patients with WNV infection; chart review using CDC’s WNV neuroinvasive and non-neuroinvasive probable/confirmed case definitions;
key_findings: WNV neuroinvasive disease (WNND) occurred in 71 out of 86 patients, including encephalitis/meningoencephalitis (WNE), meningitis without encephalitis, AFP, or transverse myelitis
Women with WNND: WNE; Men had 66% of WNND cases and a median age of 67
Patients ≥50 years old and those with at least one CCI comorbidity had higher rates of WNND, including WNE
WNV neuroinvasive disease resulted significantly more in men (47/71) who were over 50(57/71)
The presence of 3 or more Charlson Comorbidity Index components increased the risk of WNND (aOR = 19.9; 95% CI = 2.78-421)
Chronic kidney disease, alcohol use disorder, or immunocompromised status significantly increased the risk for WNND and especially WNE (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] = 6.76; 95% CI = 0.76-175)
brief.discussion: The study provides valuable insights into the risk factors associated with WNND in adults within a specific healthcare system. The findings suggest that older age, male sex, and comorbidities such as chronic kidney disease and immunocompromised status are significant predictors of WNND.
brief.limitations: This study only considered patients from one health care system.
brief.recommendations: The results of this study emphasize the importance of awareness for healthcare professionals about the risk factors associated with WNV neuroinvasive disease. Further studies should also consider the limitations of this study and how to expand beyond a single healthcare institution, and more broadly across communities and locations.

brief.summary: A 66-year-old kidney transplant recipient in South Carolina developed West Nile virus (WNV) encephalitis, despite minimal mosquito exposure. His symptoms included high-grade fever and altered mental status. After a prolonged hospital stay, he made a partial neurological recovery but eventually lost his renal graft due to the disease progression.
brief.objective: To report a rare case of recipient-acquired WNV encephalitis in a renal allograft recipient and review current management strategies and pertinent literature.
brief.timeline_geography: South Carolina, September 2024, North America (after 1999)
brief.population_sample: 66-year-old man, kidney transplant recipient
brief.key_methods: Immunosuppression minimization by discontinuing mycophenolate mofetil and continued prednisone. Intravenous immunoglobulin administration for 5 consecutive days.
key_findings: WNV encephalitis confirmed by CSF PCR
Prolonged hospital stay with partial neurological recovery but eventual graft loss
Patient had minimal mosquito exposure, making transmission less likely
brief.discussion: WNV is an arthropod-borne flavivirus transmitted primarily through mosquitoes (Culex spp.). Humans are incidental hosts. In immunocompromised patients like SOT recipients, antibody responses can be delayed or absent, and viremia may be prolonged, making CSF PCR a more useful diagnostic tool.
brief.limitations: This case report presents one isolated instance of WNV encephalitis in an SOT recipient; therefore, its results cannot be generalized to the broader population. The patient’s specific symptoms and immune status may have contributed to his disease progression.
brief.recommendations: Due to varying vector ecology in different regions, screening for WNV should remain a seasonal concern. This case highlights the importance of close monitoring in immunocompromised patients, especially those receiving organ transplants.

brief.summary: The study explores the binding and folding behavior of the flavivirus NS2B/NS3 protease, using topology-based modeling to understand how the G4SG4 linker affects complex stability.
brief.objective: To investigate the coupled binding and folding mechanism of the NS2B/NS3 protease using calibrated topology-based models and long molecular dynamics simulations.
brief.timeline_geography: Simulation data not specified in text; assuming a computational study without geographical context.
brief.population_sample: Unlinked WNV NS2B/NS3 protease, specific linked protease constructs (G4SG4)4 and (G4SG4)16.
brief.key_methods: Topology-based Gō modeling, molecular dynamics simulations, conformational space network (CSN) analysis.
key_findings: The calibrated Gō model can maintain the stability of the complex by balancing native interactions and conformational flexibility.
The G4SG4 linker's long-range interactions destabilize the NS2BC hairpin due to entropy costs for extended conformations.
Four independent folding pathways observed in refolding simulations, with 51/64 runs leading to fully bound and folded states (I1-I6).
Multiple parallel folding pathways identified through CSN analysis, providing insights into coupled binding and folding mechanisms.

brief.summary: This study analyzed the population structure of Culex pipiens mosquitoes and found that ecotypes, Wolbachia infection, and urbanization shape their genetic diversity. The results have implications for understanding the ecology and evolution of mosquito-borne diseases such as West Nile virus.
brief.objective: To investigate the genetic structure of Culex pipiens mosquitoes in a West Nile virus hotspot and to determine the effects of ecotypes, Wolbachia infection, and urbanization on their population dynamics.
brief.timeline_geography: 2022, West Nile virus hotspot
brief.population_sample: 231 Culex pipiens s.s. individuals collected from 24 trapping locations
brief.key_methods: Molecular confirmation of species identity via SNP calling and quality filtering, Genome-wide Principal Component Analysis (PCA) and ADMIXTURE to assess population structure, Detection of chromosomal inversions using windowed PCA
key_findings: Culex pipiens s.s. individuals exhibit a U-shaped pattern in genome-wide PCA, indicating ecotype differentiation
Three chromosomal inversions were identified, with frequencies ranging from 16.8% to 74.4%
Low genome-wide divergence and incomplete genetic isolation between ecotypes
brief.discussion: The observed population structure is consistent with previous studies on Culex pipiens populations. The presence of polymorphic chromosomal inversions suggests that these regions may be under diversifying selection.
brief.limitations: The sample size was relatively small, which may have affected the accuracy of the results. Additionally, the study relied on a limited number of trapping locations.
brief.recommendations: Future studies should investigate the functional significance of the identified chromosomal inversions and their role in shaping population structure.

brief.summary: The study reveals that the paraspeckle protein NONO is essential for establishing an effective antiviral immune response through chromatin regulation.
brief.objective: To determine if the absence of Noncoding nuclear occupied Nucleoskeleton associated (NONO) impacts the replication and innate immune response to viruses, particularly orthoflaviviruses.
brief.population_sample: Human A549 cells
brief.key_methods: CRISPR/Cas9 was used for knockout NONO gene in cell lines. Ruxolitinib, a JAK inhibitor, was implemented to block innate immune signaling.
key_findings: Loss of NONO increased viral replication of several mosquito- and tick-borne orthoflaviviruses
Impaired expression of IFNB1, IL-6 mRNAs in WNV-infected NONO KO cells compared to WT controls
Phenotypic data showed reduced signaling for multiple ISGs following NONO deletion.

brief.summary: This study investigates the presence of autoantibodies neutralizing type I interferons in patients infected with West Nile virus (WNV) and finds that these autoantibodies are rare in asymptomatic individuals.
brief.objective: The objective of this study is to investigate the prevalence of autoantibodies neutralizing type I interferons in WNV-infected individuals, including those with asymptomatic infection, neuroinvasive disease, and self-limiting illness.
brief.timeline_geography: patients from seven new cohorts enrolled at three centers in Italy, one center in Austria, one center in Hungary, one center in Israel, and one center in Texas, USA, between 2002 and 2024, with blood donation samples taken within 18 days of clinical disease onset or during virological screening.
brief.population_sample: 225 patients hospitalized for life-threatening WNVD, as well as 61 patients with self-limiting illness (WNVF) and 32 individuals with recent asymptomatic infection (WNVIC).
brief.key_methods: ELISA to detect autoantibodies against IFN-α2, IFN-β, or IFN-ω; luciferase-based assay to assess neutralizing activity.
key_findings: WNV-infected individuals, especially those with neuroinvasive disease, had high levels of autoantibodies that can neutralize type I interferons (IFNs). However, these autoantibodies were rare in asymptomatic WNV-infected individuals. The prevalence of autoantibodies neutralizing IFN-ω was 3%.
The results suggest a role for autoantibodies in the pathogenesis of WNV infection, particularly in neuroinvasive disease.
No differences were observed between WNVIC and WNVD patient groups, despite significant geographic variations in age distributions and proportions of male subjects among cohorts.
brief.discussion: The high levels of autoantibodies neutralizing IFNs found in WNV-infected individuals, especially those with neuroinvasive disease, suggest a potential role for these antibodies in the pathogenesis of infection. Given that only 3% of asymptomatic individuals had autoantibodies that can neutralize IFN-ω, it is possible that chronic IFN suppression may contribute to increased susceptibility or severity in WNV-infected patients.
brief.limitations: The study has several limitations, including the use of cross-sectional data from a limited number of cohorts and the potential for geographic variations in age distributions and proportions of male subjects. Additionally, the mechanisms underlying the relationship between autoantibodies and disease severity remain unclear.
brief.recommendations: Future studies should investigate the relationship between autoantibody levels and disease severity or risk of mortality in WNV-infected patients. Additionally, efforts to develop treatments targeting IFN inhibition may be warranted.

brief.summary: Researchers investigated the impact of temperature and relative humidity on the toxicity of deltamethrin and malathion to Culex quinquefasciatus mosquitoes.
brief.objective: To assess how changes in temperature (20 °C, 27 °C) and relative humidity (20%, 50%, 80%) affect the toxicity of deltamethrin and malathion to Culex quinquefasciatus mosquitoes, identifying potential limitations for control measures.
brief.timeline_geography: Not explicitly stated, but conducted in a controlled laboratory setting with temperature and humidity chambers.
brief.population_sample: Culex quinquefasciatus mosquitoes (CMAVE strain)
brief.key_methods: WHO tube bioassays with mosquito exposure to deltamethrin or malathion under different temperature and relative humidity conditions, analyzed using generalized linear models.
key_findings: Deltamethrin toxicity increased at lower relative humidities (20%, 50% compared to standard 80%) but decreased temperature had a lesser effect
Malathion toxicity showed a strong positive temperature coefficient with no significant relative humidity dependence
